It might sound cliché, but this is the first time I’m genuinely using the term hidden gem — this place truly surprised me with how good it was in every aspect.

The restaurant is spacious with two different sections being available. One is AC with high chair seatings and a bar plus DJ space too and the other is Non AC causal seatings with pool table in the center and a nice bar. Loved the use of the space and the wall designs as it looked really happening. Currently as IPL is going on they have decorated the Non AC section with team flags and have kept a big screen too.

The menu here is vast and they have options available in Indian, Asian, Italian and some more cuisines. Right now they have added a limited edition mango menu too. Apart from this they have various offers in food and drinks specially for big groups for IPL season. Prices are at par with similar type of brands and the quantity served is good.

Went here on a Monday dinner and the kitchen service was on time and table service by staff Mantu was great as he was polite and knew the menu well.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Jamaican Jerk Spice Chicken Tikka -
Served in a unique way as hanging skewers in the Dubai frame. Served with buttery naan, onion and green chutney this was juicy chicken tikkas done in green Jamaican spices. Loved the taste of this as it was not the regular tikka and the spices had nice hint of hotness to it.

Genkai Prawns Maki Roll -
Surprisingly a very nice and tasty sushi served. Fresh prawns rolled nicely with rice and the crunchy tempura coating with spicy sauce tasted excellent. Loved everything about this sushi as it was bang on tasty.

MAINS~
Mushroom & Truffle Cream Cheese Flatbread -
Thin base topped with generous amount of cheese, mushrooms, red chillies, cream cheese and sprayed with aromatic and earthy truffle oil looked perfect and tasted delicious. Loved the juicy mushrooms and the cream cheese and they were honest in using the truffle oil hence a perfect dish again.

Nasi Goreng -
This was a complete miss for me as it was way different from the Nasi Goreng that I have been eating for years. Maybe it is their way as I felt it was a plain normal fried rice however being fried rice it tasted nice but for Nasi Goreng they need to check the recipe.

DESSERT~
Mango Cheesecake -
Again a very different version of cheesecake as this was more closer to a baked layered malai cake with mango flavour and topped with Alphonse mango. Taste wise it was really good as the mango was sweet and it was not extra sweet.

MOCKTAILS~
Tropical Bliss.
Sunset Bloom.
Both the mocktails tasted refreshing as the ingredients tasted nice with each other.

So our meal at What’s Your Plan was really good as the food tasted perfect, the ambiance plus vibe of the restaurant is great and the service was excellent. An iconic Mumbai café with a lively vibe and historic charm. Great place to relax after Colaba Causeway shopping—food is decent, drinks are good, and the atmosphere is the real highlight.

Leopold Cafe is worth visiting for its history and energetic ambience. The food is average for the price, but the experience, crowd, and location make it a must-visit spot in South Mumbai.

Very vibrant and famous place with lots of character. Can be crowded and slightly overpriced, but still worth a visit at least once for the iconic Mumbai café experience.

📍 About the Place
Leopold Cafe is one of Mumbai’s oldest and most famous cafés, founded in 1871 and located on Colaba Causeway — right across from the Colaba Police Station. It’s a cultural landmark as well as a popular hangout for tourists, locals, and fans of the novel Shantaram.

The café also carries historical significance because it was one of the spots attacked during the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, and some bullet marks remain preserved as a memorial.

🍽️ Ambience & Atmosphere
Vibe:
Lively, bustling, and full of character — a bit of an old-school vibe with a mix of retro and bohemian decor.

Great people-watching spot after a shopping stroll along Colaba Causeway.

Often packed, especially in evenings and weekends — queues are common

🍔 Food & Drinks — What People Say
Positives:
Wide, varied menu with continental, Indian, Chinese & bar food options.

Popular items include beer towers, shepherd’s pie, walnut pie, chocolate desserts, chicken wings, burgers and more.

Some reviewers have enjoyed refreshing drinks like Coke floats and milkshakes.

Cost:
Expect mid-range pricing — around ₹2500 for two people including drinks (approx.) with alcohol.

🧑‍🍳 Service & Crowd
What reviewers note:
✔ Friendly, helpful staff when it’s not crowded.
⚠ Can be slow or inattentive during peak hours.
⚠ Busy weekends and evenings often have lines and waiting times.

📌 Pro Tips Before You Go
This cafe is worth visiting for the experience and atmosphere, even if the food opinions vary.

Best to visit earlier in the day or on weekdays to avoid long waits.

reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Sea princess, a renowned hotel in Juhu from years now which is known for its hospitality came up with this restaurant Jeon on its ground floor and gave an opportunity to people other than their Inhouse guests too to experience this lavish restaurant serving many of the delicious items with their wide ranged buffet menu. Right from the entrance upto the exit, everything was a nice experience.

The place is very well designed keeping many things in mind. The seating is very comfortable and spacious unlike we often experience at buffet place. The price of 1600 INR for the weekday dinner gets you a full fledged meal from soups, chaat counter, salad bar, live pasta and delicacies from North India, mughlai and Asia.

Non-veg Starters had chicken cajun which had tender chicken well greased and tossed to crisp and tawa fry basa which is barely found anywhere coz basa is soft and people find it real hard to tawa fry such soft fish but here at Jeon, It wasn't just tawa fried but was fried to perfection with right marination making it all the more Delicious.

Veg starters: veg crispy and paneer tikka which was fresh and soft very well marinated and grilled. It went well with the chutney served alongside

Loved pani puri served here with options to select from ragda or potato and sprouts.

Salad bar options can get better with more choices of essentials for health freaks.

The Chef at pasta counter made us a white sauce pasta which was super yum. Specially the bread severs with it was too good.

Mains: A wide spread counter focusing on mains unlike other bunches I have attended recently where their focus is Mainly on starters. Their dal makhani Cannot be missed. Mutton rara was something I couldn't hold onto after first bite. It was lamb cooked at its best and softness. They had items to suit all taste buds from domestic to international.

Desserts : someone who designer the buffet menu at Jeon must be dessert lover for they have given special attention to the desssert counter which was surprisingly bigger than the main course counter with so many options for anyone to go Gaga. While it's practically impossible to try so many items, some of what I witnessed here was blueberry pie, apple streusel, sago pudding, choclate orange marmalade, carrot cake, dual pannacotta, strawberry jelly, and some more.

Vegetarian Spread

The main course had a wide choice of vegetables and freshly made Indian flatbreads/rotis.
The highlight was the Banjara Special Dal paired with rice, along with traditional Rajasthani khichadi that added an authentic touch.
Desserts were a treat on their own – ghewar, imarti with rabdi, cupcakes, mud cakes, and chocolate mousse, each prepared with great attention to taste and presentation.

Non-Vegetarian Spread

In the main course, we enjoyed a rich chicken curry, flavourful fish curry, and the standout smoked/dum chicken biryani, which had just the right balance of aroma and spices.

Ambience & Entertainment

To top it all off, the live singer performing 90s Hindi classics created a nostalgic and soothing atmosphere. It elevated the entire dining experience and made our anniversary feel even more special.

Overall Experience

Go early (lunch/dinner) to avoid peak crowd and ensure you get the full buffet spread without items running out.

Try out your best veg and non veg dishes - one at a time so that you don't get confused.
Start with the live counters (pani puri, kebabs) and work your way to mains & desserts — being strategic helps when you want to make the most of a buffet.

Bring your foodie group or family — the place has big seating which is great for group bookings.

In short: if you’re in Mumbai’s Western Suburbs and on the lookout for an unlimited food buffet restaurant that is within your budget, this is very much worth a visit. What We Ordered

Our feast included a fantastic mix of seafood, meats, and sides:

- Crab Kakori

- Shallow Fried Malvani Bombil

- Chicken Chilli

- Chicken Malvani Masala

- Prawns Bhujane

- APC Pomfret & APC Crab

- Pasta Arrabiata for kids

- Rice Bhakri, Ghavane, Wade

- Solkadi

Everything was rich, flavorful, and well-prepared, especially the seafood, which was fresh and cooked to perfection.

Service Excellence

Special shout-out to Chandani, Chandan, and Roshan, they took exceptional care of us from start to finish. For a table of 10, the service was quick, warm, and always attentive. They made excellent suggestions and ensured every dietary need was handled with care.

Price & Value

Medium to high priced considering the generous portions and seafood quality. Value for money for group dining with great ambiance.

-Verdict

A must-visit for seafood lovers and anyone wanting a coastal food experience with a modern twist. We had a table reservation for 9:45 PM and arrived by 9:55 PM. Despite being just 10 minutes late, we were made to wait another 10 minutes before being seated—even though we could clearly see 4–5 empty tables inside. This initial delay set the tone for what turned out to be an underwhelming evening.

Once seated, we weren’t provided with menus until we asked for them. After deciding on our soups and starters, no server approached us for over 10 minutes, prompting me to personally request someone to take our order. There was no water on the table, and even after requesting it, the server simply forgot—walking past our table multiple times to serve others. Eventually, I had to approach someone who seemed to be the manager, only to be told, repeatedly, that “the staff is busy” and we needed to “co-operate.” Frankly, it doesn’t take much effort to bring menus, take an order, or serve water—basic expectations at any restaurant.

As for the food:

Soups: The Manchow soup was lukewarm and seemed like it came straight from the buffet, with soggy fried noodles on the side. The Tomato soup, on the other hand, had a nice basil flavor and was decent.

Starters: The Paneer Chilly was flavorful and enjoyable. Among the non-veg options, the Korean Fried Chicken had an odd fishy smell, although the sauce was good. The Pan Fried Chicken Momos were tasty, though the accompanying dip was overly sweet.

Main Course: The Chicken Tikka Masala and assorted breads were well-prepared and satisfying. However, the Chicken Biryani was disappointing—bland and lacking any real depth of flavor. The vegetarian mains—Vegetable Stir Fry in Hot Garlic Sauce and Pink Pasta—were good but took an unusually long time to arrive.

Mocktails: We tried the No-jito, a twist on the classic mojito, which didn’t stand out, and the Guava Mary, which was refreshing and enjoyable.

No desserts were ordered, mainly because by the end of the meal, our patience was running thin.

Overall, the dining experience was marred by disorganized service, inattentive staff, and inconsistent food quality. While a few dishes did manage to impress, they weren’t enough to outweigh the frustrating delays and lack of basic hospitality. For a restaurant that seems to take pride in its offerings, the service fell severely short.

The restaurant is spacious with a mini and a full sized bar. The ambiance is super bright with tribal decor touch. Loved the colours used everywhere and every corner looks really beautiful. The menu contains global dishes with sone traditional Indian food being available too. Loved the menu as you get everything from sushi to chicken tikka is available in their menu. Prices are at par with similar type of brands and the quantity served is nice. Also they do run dining offers so check online before visiting.

Golden Prawn Tempura Roll -
Again one of the best sushi experiences. Their portion is 5 pieces so you will definitely crave more. Crunchy tempura, fresh prawns, spicy sauce and everything in this sushi was perfect.

MAINS~
Wild Mushroom & Truffle Cacio E Pepe -
Man. This was one of the best pasta I have ever had. Earthy flavours due to mushrooms and truffle oil. Perfectly done spaghetti with crunchy veggies and the watery cheese sauce was outstanding. Try it to believe it.

Prawn Ghee Pepper Roast with Tadka Lemon Coriander Rice -
Fresh prawns in ghee roast gravy tasted good. The rice went nicely however I am not a fan of whole coriander hence full marks for gravy.

DESSERT~
Slow Baked Chocolate Bar -
This wasn’t that great as the chocolate used was not that tasty.

MOCKTAILS~
Black & Yellow.
Tropical Delight.
Both the drinks had perfect taste.

We visited Agrezi Dhaba on Saturday, 31st May 2025, as a group of 3 married couples along with 2 kids, hoping for a pleasant evening out. Unfortunately, the experience turned out to be an utter disappointment from start to finish.

First of all, imagine walking into a restaurant on a Saturday night and seeing only two waiters managing the entire floor. That alone sets the tone for what’s to come. Service was painfully slow and chaotic, with one waiter literally sprinting from table to table trying to handle everything. It felt like watching a poorly managed event, not a professional dining experience.

I had made a booking through Zomato, only to be told by the waiter that pricing would differ if we paid via the app compared to paying directly. Why play such shady pricing games with customers? This kind of misleading marketing is simply unacceptable.

To make matters worse, some of my friends ordered from the bar, only to be told they were out of Blenders Pride by 9:30 PM. On a Saturday night? That’s basic stock management gone wrong.

Then came the confusing bar menu experience. The waiter actually insisted we decide how many pegs we were going to drink upfront because only then we’d be given a certain rate. Who does that? It’s ridiculous to expect guests to decide their entire order before even settling in. The pricing for single, 6-pegs, and 12-pegs was all over the place and made no sense at all.

The hospitality was shockingly poor. Since we had two young kids, we requested Wi-Fi so they could watch cartoons while the adults had dinner. There was no mobile network coverage, and the Wi-Fi was denied. The reason? According to the manager, sharing Wi-Fi would crash their system. Honestly, it was laughable—we actually joked about it being the “joke of the year.” This level of excuse-making is unprofessional at best.

If all this wasn’t enough, the waiter later rushed us to make the payment, standing by our table repeatedly asking “Google Pay ya cash?” When I asked for 5 minutes, his response was: “Jaldi karo, mujhe bhi ghar nikalna hai.” Absolutely unacceptable. We were still wrapping up our night and he made it feel like we were being kicked out. If there’s a rule that bills must be settled before midnight, then inform guests clearly in advance—not after pressuring them in the middle of their meal.

As for the food, it was bland, overpriced, and underwhelming. For a bill of ₹8500, we expected much better quality and taste. It felt like basic food dressed up with fancy pricing.

In short, Agrezi Dhaba completely ruined our Saturday night outing. Poor service, rude staff, lack of basic amenities, and average food at inflated prices.

The vibe is unapologetically unpretentious. No Instagrammable neon signs or overpriced fusion tapas here. Just solid, top-notch bar food that hits the spot every single time. The chicken lollypop,crispy, the chicken fried rice, the kebab starters— everything’s consistently great.

Simply amazing hospitality and such pretty restaurants. This Infact, was my reason to visit Nawab Saheb for their ongoing Tawa & Tandoor Festival (20th- 28th September) as there are very few restaurants who actually go out of their way to curate special menus like these. Brainchild of Chef Yunus Khan, I think everything on the menu was fantastic. Service was slow as the restaurant was quite packed, being a Friday night. I opted for the vegetarian fare priced at 2800. Frankly, I thought it was value for money only because of the main course. Just their dal makhani and paneer will leave you licking your fingers till the end. Here's what the spread consisted of and how I felt about it :
Vegetarian :
1. Til Malai ka Phool (5/5)- Melt in the mouth brocolli with cream cheese. Found the cauliflower okayish.
2. Chef Yunus Khan ka Paneer Tikka (10/5)- Star dish! Has to be the best I've had in a long time. Highly recommended.
3. Subz ki Ashraphiya (3/5)- Found it average.
4. Bhune Bhutte ke Seekh (5/5)- AMAZING combination of seekh Kebab and babycorn. YUM.
5. Kabuki Kebab (3/5)- Found it too dry. Taste wise as well, bland due to Chickpeas.
6. Chukunder ke Kebab (4/5)- Beetroot galauti, it was nice.
7. Kumbh ke Galawat (5/5)- Wow. Has to be the one thing I'd come back for! Surprisingly it was served on a thepla kind of bread.
8. Aloo Atishi (4/5)- Bharwan aloo, classic.

Mains :
1. Paneer Kaliyan (10/5)- Now that's what I'm talking about. It's dishes like these that make you remember these hotels. No one does mains like them. I ALWAYS skip mains but yesterday I was too tempted after a bite and ended up having 3 pieces of bread after such heavy array of starters. MY FAVOURITE FROM YESTERDAY because it was cashew gravy, so creamy, soft paneer chunks and rightly spiced. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
2. Daal Nawab (10/5)- Probably as good as the one I've had in Delhi at ITC. Properly slow cooked for 48 hours, perfectly creamy and texture was just right. Not overdone. Yum.
3. Subz Biryani - couldn't dare to try it. Was too full.

Desserts : Assorted variety
Motichoor Laddoo, Kaju Katli, Kalakand, Gulab Jamun, Akhroti Halwa, Phirni - all were great but my favourites were the Phirni and Gulab Jamun.

Great staff and great hospitality by team. Special thanks to Manager Avanish, steward Shrikant and Chef Rahul Karve., name_person=Mahek Khanna}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Nawab Saheb as the name suggests it’s a luxurious fine dine restaurant located in the basement of Renaissance Powai. Nawabi Aloo Ki Nazakat

Chef Yunus Khan Ka Paneer

Jheenga-e- Nisha

Décor: 5/5

Value for Money: 5/5

P.S: The review is strictly depending on my personal experience., name_person=shripad marathe}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=3 years ago, review=Nawab Sahab - Westin Powai
Amazing place , richness all over , menu curated by master Chef Yunus Khan a fusion of awadh , frontier India and Rajasthan
This place is known for it's Kebabs and mouth watering aromatic curries

Here is what we had :
==================

Veg and non veg platter - makai motiya seekh minced corn charred with Indian spices normally served on skewers. Since it was a platter it was a single piece
YONUS KHAN KA PANEER TIKKA - signature dish. Middle had a filling of dry fruits and nuts. Indian spices tandoor well with spices balanced
Subz gauloti - melt in mouth minced veggies with herbs and spices served over a bread. So Lucknow ( must try )
MALAI KA PHOOL - richness all over . Cheese and cream marinated broccoli charred.
Perfect

Non veg platter - Mahira babuli kebab famous dish of amritsar on bones. Melt in mouth tangy spicy marinating. Must try
GALAWAT KE KEBAB - do try this , served on a small paratha. Minced lamb with spices .balanced was prefect. Normally served on a griddle. Since it was a platter just had one piece which was enough to know the culinary talent of the master chef.

Samunder ki apsara - wow this was something new . Small lobster tandoor to perfection. Special spices used by the chef. I will remember this . Never had it as a starter

Coming to mains :
VEG - do try the Aminamadi  Saag , a spinach preparation with garlic and cumin. Freshly made full of flavours. Chef has kept it simple . Let the dish do the talking

Paneer Lazeez e khaas again a signature by chef. Chunks of cottage cheese with rich tomato gravy . Subtle in spices and aromatic at the same time.
However the 48 hour Long process Dal e yunus is worth a wait , rich urad lentil. Goes well with biryani or breads.

Non veg - ghost nihari tho banta hai boss . Bone marrow stock , lamb slowly cooked gives that aromatic taste and flavour.
Do try the murg handi lazeez - braised chicken with base of onion gravy along with methi ( fenugreek ) and cream. Chicken was cooked well tender and juicy

Must say that food , kebab or the gravy are not heavy or oily. Just perfect.
Missed out the prawns kasundi , lovely hit of kasundi cooked well. Velvety tomato and anar gravy. Do try.

Small portion of Subz Chilman biryani , long grain basmati rice with saffron a bit of Ittar ghee and veggies

Breads - Taftaan / Khameeri / Naan
However the dessert had a pleasant surprise
Had a capsicum halwa FOR the first time.
Something different which one needs to try out

Overall experience = awesome
Felt like a Nawab Dining at this place paired with a sparkling wine

Big thanks to Saurabh Dixit and team Westin for hosting

Ps. Only drawback , could not meet the master chef as had a day Off
Next time for sure

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very quiet}, time_line=4 months ago, review=5-Star Review for Tamnak Thai, Dadar Shivaji Park

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)

Tamnak Thai in Dadar Shivaji Park, Mumbai, has solidified its place as my absolute favorite Thai restaurant after multiple delightful visits, with my latest being on September 1, 2025. Nestled on Veer Savarkar Marg opposite Starbucks, this spot offers an authentic Thai escape with its warm, oriental ambiance—think elegant sculptures, soft lighting, and spacious seating that feels like a trip to Bangkok. The staff, including our attentive server who expertly guided us through the menu, delivered courteous and efficient service, enhancing the cozy in-house experience at Table No. 5. The absence of a service charge is a thoughtful bonus in Mumbai’s dining scene.
Our meal began with refreshing drinks that set the tone perfectly. The Cinderella mocktail (₹460) was a delightful blend of tropical fruitiness with a fizzy twist—light, sweet, and utterly refreshing. Paired with it, the Himalayan mineral water (₹140 per bottle, 2 bottles at ₹280 total) offered a crisp, pure hydration that complemented the flavors ahead. The Iced Tea (₹240) brought a chilled, subtly sweet note, while the Kiwi Kooler (₹460) burst with fresh kiwi and a tropical fizz, and the Virgin Mojito (₹460) delivered a classic minty-lime zing—each generously portioned and served promptly.
For appetizers, the Phad Khi-Mao Kung (stir-fried prawns with basil and chilies, ₹1040) was a spicy masterpiece, with juicy prawns and holy basil creating a bold, aromatic dish. The Satay Kai (chicken satay skewers, ₹860) featured tender, perfectly grilled meat with a creamy peanut sauce that balanced sweet and spicy notes flawlessly. Mains were a highlight, starting with the Tom Yam Kai (chicken Tom Yum soup, ₹520) and Tom Yam Kung (prawn version, ₹560), both tart and fragrant with lemongrass and chilies, warming us up delightfully. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Butterfly High, Vikhroli truly lives up to its name — high on vibes, high on food, and high on presentation.

Overview
AER at the Four Seasons is a rooftop experience that lives up to the hype. Perched high above Worli, it delivers sweeping Mumbai skyline and sea views, a modern yet warm ambience, and consistently polished service — ideal for both special evenings and relaxed drinks with friends.

Ambience & design
- Incredible vantage point: panoramic views of Mumbai and the Arabian Sea are the star — especially dramatic when clouds roll in or the city lights up at night.
- Roof engineering: the covered rooftop feels state-of-the-art — thoughtfully designed to shelter guests during rain while preserving the sense of openness. Even in a downpour the space felt airy and comfortable, with rain adding to the drama rather than disrupting the experience.
- Vibe: stylish, contemporary décor with an upscale lounge energy. Music, lighting and layout encourage both intimate conversations and lively groups without feeling crowded.

Drinks
- Negroni: expertly executed — perfectly blanched (clean, balanced bitterness and bright aromatics), with excellent temperature and presentation. The cocktail showcased strong technique and attention to classic proportions.
- Cocktail program: creative but respectful of classics; bartenders clearly know their craft and tailor drinks to taste.

Food
- Guacamole prepared tableside: a highlight. Watching it made fresh added theatre, and the result was vibrant, aromatic and packed with flavour — creamy texture, bright citrus and just the right seasoning. Superb balance of richness and acidity.
- Overall tasting: dishes leaned modern, high-quality and well-seasoned. Portions are geared for sharing and designed to complement the cocktail-led experience.

Service
- Attentive and professional without being intrusive. Staff handled the evening smoothly, from timing of drinks and food to accommodating the rain cover without fuss.
- Knowledgeable servers and bartenders willing to recommend pairings and adjust drinks to preference.

Pros
- Unmatched views and rooftop atmosphere.
- Weather-proofed design that keeps the rooftop enjoyable even in rain.
- High-caliber cocktails and memorable live-prep elements (e.g., guacamole).
- Polished, thoughtful service.

Cons / notes
- Popularity means it can get busy; reservations are recommended for prime seating.
- Price point is upscale — expect to pay a premium for the location and experience.

Who it’s for
- Couples seeking a romantic, skyline-backed evening.
- Groups celebrating special occasions.
- Cocktail enthusiasts who appreciate skilled bartending and well-executed classics.

Bottom line
AER at the Four Seasons is a standout rooftop destination in Mumbai. The service was excellent — greeted at the entrance, escorted to our table, and consistently checked on throughout the meal. The staff were attentive, quick with refills, cutlery changes, and serving food. Honestly, the 7% service charge felt justified.

We ordered quite a few items:

• Crab Soup – extremely dense, rich, and flavourful.
• Starters – tasty but small portion sizes, especially the meat pieces.
• Ghee Roast Chicken – beautifully balanced ghee and spices.
• Mangalorean Pepper Roast Mutton – thick, spicy chilli mix; delicious but avoid the chillies if you prefer mild heat.
• Prawns Balchao – tangy, well-spiced, served with poi that paired perfectly.

Mains:
• Kori Roti – traditional dry roti with desi chicken curry. Best enjoyed by crushing the roti into the gravy.
• Anna’s Curry – the standout dish of the night. Mild, flavourful curry served with your choice of fish; pairs great with neer dosa or rice.
• Pullimunchi – for spice lovers; a bold, sour and spicy thick red gravy.

We also ordered the Pomfret and Surmai Thalis, which included fried fish, fish curry, rasam, sambar, rice, neer dosa, payasam, papad, and chutneys. The only disappointment was that all three fish curries came with head pieces — for the price, a better cut was expected.

Pricing is slightly on the higher side, but you can check dining apps for discounts to make it more reasonable.

Must-tries: Crab Soup, Ghee Roast Chicken, and Anna’s Curry., name_person=Suhel Shaikh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Benne_Dosa], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=Edited 2 months ago, review=Location: Located in the Times Square Building & is very easy to navigate and reach. Have seen many big family unions / office get togethers at this restaurant as it caters to both young,adult and elderly with its extensive but delicious food menu.
Food: We had been to this place multiple times in the last one month and most of the dishes were consistently good in taste except for a few. Need to note that the breakfast items could be unavailable in the evening and night. We had tried most of their vegetarian dishes and mocktails. Although the mocktails were less in options,all of them are crafted to elevate one's dining experience. Their southern mogu mogu,Nerula neer are must try. Coming to food, their starters/appetizers variety is wide with South Indian appetizers (like pepper roast,ghee roast, benne dosa, pazham pori and rasam wade), Tandoor items, Continental (french fries, nachos) and Asian appetizers (chilli paneer is a must try here). Main course had simple and healthy options like choosing a curry along with Indian breads (Appam, Idiyappam parathas et. Also, inpite of a large crowd waiting for the restaurant,none of the customers were hurried to pay & leave. Thanks for the management to be considerate and polite all the time.
Restroom: There's a restroom for men,women separately but not much space to handle kids in the restroom. Nevertheless , the restroom is well maintained and clean.
Kid-friendly: They have a baby chair for families with toddlers. They were considerate when we ordered a small portion from their papad basket, a scoop of ice cream for our kid.

Let me start with what they dare to call a Feta Salad – a sad mess of wilted lettuce dumped in a bowl, tossed with exactly one (yes, one!) lonely crumb of feta. You know it’s bad when even the croutons taste defeated.

The final straw was the Aglio Olio – a dish that’s meant to be simple and comforting. Instead, what arrived was a dry, clumpy mess that required us to literally use our own olive oil and dressing just to make it semi-edible. After a few bites of that, we gave up and dumped the rest of the food in the bin. Yes, it was that bad.

Definitely visiting again!\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Lunch\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b9800\u20131,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Quiet, easy to talk\",\"GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE\":[\"Suitable_for_all_group_sizes\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Bhavin Parekh\",\"time_line\":\"2 months ago\",\"review\":\"It\u2019s the relaunched version (2.0) of Joshi House (formerly in Bandra) now in Worli Koliwada. The emphasis is now strongly on Indian regional flavours (especially coastal & Rajasthani). The place is visually striking with good lighting, atmosphere within gives both grandeur and warmth. The space is spread over three floors, each with a distinct mood.\\n\u2022 Ground floor has al fresco seating (patio style), greenery, the entrance has terracotta pots, Jaisalmer stone jaali screens.\\n\u2022 First floor is more formal dining: yellow cement flooring, textured walls, sculptural wood furniture. Softer, more calming.\\n\u2022 Second floor / Bar area: moodier, more intimate. Deep hues (violet walls, etc.), vaulted ceilings, artistic murals (e.g. hand\u2011painted tiger motifs).\\nDetails of Rajasthani heritage show up subtly in decor: brass, stone, carved wood, warm earthy textures - feels lived\u2011in, comfortable.\\nThe cuisine is rooted in Indian regional flavours, especially coastal and Rajasthani. Sea food gets centre stage. Vegetarian fare isn\u2019t an afterthought. Top dishes like Balinese bhel, Dabeli sliders, Sweet potato shammi chaat (must try), Thecha brie toast, Mushroom benne dosa,Truffle Palak Saag with burrata along with makai roti, Beetroot malai kofta along with Malbari parotta etc get good attention. Desserts get creative - the Ghevar (Rajasthani dessert), Paan Magnum Kulfi etc. Nostalgic yet with some innovations. Cocktail and Mocktail is robust: creative mocktails like Sunset sipper, Berry almond mingle, Pom rajwadi, etc. are flavourful and refreshing.\\nService is generally attentive, with staff that understand the menu, guide and explains regional flavours. Joshi House Worli is a strong evolution from its Bandra version - more rooted, more coherent in theme, more local (both in ingredients and aesthetics). If you appreciate ambience, design, and wanting to explore awesome regional Indian cuisine with flair, it's a great pick. For special occasions or a nice evening out, it\u2019s well worth it.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Nidhi jain\",\"time_line\":\"3 weeks ago\",\"review\":\"Loved the place very much. It was perfect for lunch as well as dinner. They have set menu which is totally worth a try. I had tried their starters in vegetarian and I loved their thecha brie toast very much. It was super cheesy and delicious. It was different and worth trying . It was crispy and crunchy. The other starter I tried was their sweet potato shammi chaat and that too was delicious to taste. In main course, I tried their truffle palak saag with makai roti. The subzi was good in quantity and i also loved their innovation in this dish as they added burata cheese on the top of the gravy and the makai roti was soft and tasty. Their cocktails were worth a try. They were innovative. I tried their hazel drink and it had good taste of coffee and the other was also nice. I liked their dessert and mainly their presentation in that. I tried their kerala chocolate ganache and it was served with a sorbet which made the dessert fantastic in taste.\\nThe food was good and the service was also quick and nice.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,800\u20132,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Quiet, easy to talk\",\"GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE\":[\"2_people\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO\",\"Suitable_for_all_group_sizes\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS\":\"Highly recommend\",\"GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO\":[\"Large_vegetarian_selection\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS\":[\"Vegetarian_options\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Nikita K\",\"time_line\":\"a month ago\",\"review\":\"\u201cHuman Jaha Pe Tameez Suey Khaya Hai, Bhuke Hi Wapas Aaye Hai\u201d\\n-A go-getter Foodie.\\n\\nIf luxury had a desi heart, it would look exactly like Joshi House. In the heart of Worli, this fine dining gem is a North Indian food lover\u2019s dream \u2014 blending authentic flavours with a refined modern touch. The ambience is simply stunning \u2014 warm lights, earthy d\u00e9cor, soft music, and an old-world charm that makes you want to stay longer. The perfect spot for an indulgent evening with friends, family, or even a quiet soulful date night.\\n\\nFor mocktails, we started with the Spice Sutra and the House Special J House. Both drinks were beautifully presented \u2014 vibrant, aromatic, and bursting with layered flavours.\\n\\nFor Appetisers,  we called for Sweet Potato Shammi Chaat which was an absolute delight! The soft shammi with the sweetness of potato, dash of ice-cold ice cream (Yes! Ice Cream) layer and tang from chutneys created a perfect harmony of flavours and Chutney Avocado Toast which was a creative twist on the classic! Creamy avocado topped with tangy Indian chutneys, giving every bite a fresh and fusion-style punch.\\n\\nThe bar was already set high by the appetisers, we were looking forward for the mains now. Next we ordered Beetroot Malai Kofta Curry which was smooth, and rich. The beetroot koftas were melt-in-the-mouth soft, perfectly paired with a luscious malai gravy. Enjoyed it with Cheese Garlic Naan, which was fluffy and indulgent and Paneer Tikka Biryani which was Fragrant, flavorful, and perfectly spiced. The tender paneer tikka chunks added that royal touch, making it a must-try for every biryani lover.\\n\\nAaaaand, for desserts we chose  Joshi House Ghevar \u2013 Our absolute favourite! A stunning dessert that truly stole the show. The presentation, the textures, and the sweetness \u2014 everything was on point. A perfect modern take on a traditional Rajasthani classic. Where was this all these years?\\n\\nJoshi House truly stands out not just for its food but for the complete experience it offers \u2014 from the elegant ambience to the impeccable service. A special thanks to Francis for the warm hospitality and for making our evening truly memorable.\\n\\nSuperb food, heart-touching flavours, and that Ghevar\u2026 ahhh still thinking about it!\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Arhan Sarkar\",\"time_line\":\"2 years ago\",\"review\":\"4.0/5\\nJoshi House reminds me of a place where classical architecture meets modern art. The facade is very minimal and can be missed if you\u2019re not looking carefully. Situated on the ever so busy Pali Hill road, it is a cozy atmospheric place filled with elegance and charm. The decor is white and embroidered with carefully placed art pieces like quirky flower vases.\\n\\nFood is as expected quite exquisite. The place is quite famous for its chefs. The carefully done dishes are set apart quite easily and the touch of decadence is very satisfying. It is on the expensive side so be prepared for spending a little extra. One area i would like to see improvement is the dessert. I had ordered the raspberry and dark chocolate, pretty safe choice but i had expected a little more creativity from this department. On calling the restaurant in the afternoon about parking, the manager suddenly claimed they have “stopped online reservations” — even though the slot was available and confirmed on Google. When I asked his name (atleast thriceA) he disconnected the call without telling.
Not taking a chance, we reached at 7:30pm. The restaurant was barely 40% occupied. Our waiter Kabir was polite and helpful — full marks to him for service.
The major issue happened at billing — they flatly refused to accept Zomato payment despite Zomato showing a good discount option. There was no notice displayed, and we were not told at entry or while ordering. The manager “Shrikant Pedhnekar” was unapologetic and defensive instead of clarifying or expressing regret. While we were leaving, another manager (name unknown) also argued with us. In this era of 'Customer First', not once these managers showed any signs of being apologetic nor regret. Other aspects:
• Ambience feels dated — furniture and décor easily 15–20 years old
• Prices are comparable to premium restaurants but food is only average in taste and portion
• We ordered for two cocktails but they were not well made.
• Service charge of 10% was added automatically while most restaurants of this level charge 5% (we got it removed)
• Restaurant is on 1st floor - No lift so elderlies and people with mobility issues will find it difficult to reach the restaurant

reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=As the name suggests, a high end premium restaurant located in Atria Mall next to Matahari on level 4, South Bombay Bar was the place I wanted to revisit so eagerly. Had a fabulous experience last time around and it was no different this time around as well. I love the ambiance of the place, well spread, spacious, everyone gets their privacy, yet you always feel right in between action all the time. Just loved how they have painted the ceiling with the map of South Mumbai and well illuminated wall depicting CSTM building structure. A nice mix of high tables, couple tables, comfortable sofa seating, regular tables and chairs section for large groups, just a very well planned layout I must say.

Talking about what all I tried here at South Bombay Bar, I actually just loved everything that was called for -

We started with few appetizers - Mexican Potatoes, Cheese Chilli Garlic Bread and Cheesy Jalapeno Stuffed Mushrooms. I just loved all three of them, but a word of caution for the Mexican Potatoes. Extremely rich in flavours but the Mexican spices also do their wonder. So it's really spicy. We actually asked the chef to tone down the spices, but we still felt it was quite spicy. So those who are in love with spice, this is your treat. I am a big fan of mushrooms and when it's jalapeno and cheese stuffing, it's heavenly. Don't miss this if you eat mushrooms. Last but not the least, we feel you can't go wrong with a chilli cheese toast, but you need to get it right. And that's what you will get here, a safe bet Always.

Along with food, called for couple of drinks - one of my favorites again - Date and Saffron Frappe. I don't think you get this anywhere else and somewhere it's definitely worth travelling and coming here perhaps just for this. Must must try! Also tried the Rosemary Watermelon Iced Tea. Fresh Watermelon is always good to have and a nice blend by the bar tender. Moving on to the mains, we tried the Paneer Londonwala Meal (Tikka Masala gravy) and called for Parathas as our Indian bread option. Just loved this Paneer vegetable one of the best. Meal comes along with papad. Beautiful presentation! After this meal, we had the Dhabewali Dal Khichdi, perfectly made. Light on stomach.

Finally, for desserts - we had Sexin A Tea Pot! Interesting name but I was excited to have this gooey chocolate with vanilla Ice-cream and Orange Zest. That orange flavour right towards the end was super refreshing. Their desserts menu is fabulous - next time around I look forward to having the Blueberry Kulfi and Pinnacotta. Hopefully soon will visit once again. A sit down multi course Italian meal with Italian wine is what you witness! An experience unparalleled. Sofitel has always been my one of the most favourite places in Mumbai because of the numerous festivals they do. But the food tried at this event was one of the best that I have ever had!

Every course had its own wine, started with couple of white and finishing with couple of red! All the wines had been specially curated and imported and the food also complemented really well. You have Veg as well as Non Veg options, so one can choose accordingly. Talking about what all I tried at Sofitel Wine Days -

We began with Almond and Goat Cheese as Starters, had Zucchini, Avocado and Mustard Sauce. The non veg equivalent to this was Amaranth Prawns. This was served with the first wine of the evening - Villa Antinori Bianco - white wine. A perfect way to begin your meal! The wine aims at maximizing the Tuscan character of the wine and is straw yellow in colour with greenish highlights. It is still wine with approx 12% alcohol by volume.

Next in line we tried the Forest Mushroom Veloute which was Truffle Mousse, Pine nuts and brioche. Absolutely awesome and I loved the taste! Texture was thick and rich in flavour and aroma. This was served with the second white wine of the evening - Antinori Santa Cristina Pinot Grigio. The wine is straw yellow in colour, the wine offers fruity and delicate aromas of pineapple, green apples and lemon. The wine is refreshing and has approx 12% alcohol by volume.

Moving to the mains - we first had the Baked Courgette which was Duxelle, Edamame and Parmesan Risotto! Again an awesome dish for Mushroom lovers. This was served along with the first red wine of the evening - Antinori Santa Cristina Toscana. For non vegetarians there was Grilled Seabass (Risotto). Wine is a red wine from Toscana, Italy and has approx 12.5% alcohol by volume.

Next main dish was Grilled Polenta which had red lentil ragout, charred leek, fondant potato and caramlised onion straw! A filling dish and really good! I preferred Polenta more than Baked Courgette! This one was served along with Antinori Peppoli Chianti Classico, the last wine / 2nd red wine of the evening. Non veg equivalent was Braised Lamb Shank with same ingredients. The wine represents the Chianti Classico territory and it's historic grape variety with typical floral and fruity aromas. Wine has approx 13% alcohol by volume.

We ended our meal with one of the most amazing desserts - Berry Trail. It had Raspberry Parfait, Blueberry Jelly, Blackberry Chantilly, Oats Crumble and Berry Chocolate Crisps. One of the best dessert that I have had till date! Simply awesome.

In complete awe of the experience at Sofitel Mumbai BKC! As mentioned earlier, they keep doing #sofitelwinedays often, almost every month and I would highly recommend everyone including all wine connoisseurs!, name_person=Jatin Shah}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=Sofitel BKC  has been our favourite hub to enjoy some family times , thanks to their Festivals which they organise with great enthusiasm .

This time it was our time to be a part of their Italian Fiesta Festival at Le Bar Diamantaire which was in collaboration with Ferrari Mumbai .

Le Bar has a Classy Ambience and flaunts to be one of the rare restaurant in Mumbai having a Wine Tower of its own . What will amaze you more is the food they serve which is just too good to be missed .

Lastly Not to Forget the Red Beauty ie Ferrari standing at the door step of the Sofitel.

Let's straight move on to what all we savoured out here during our visit .

Appetizers :

Bruschetta :
An amazing start to a classy evening . Crisp bread with luscious Topping ....

Arracini Balls :
Hot balls having a Scrummy peas based stuffing .

Polenta :
Boiled Cornmeal served with a tasty mushrooms preparation served along side .

Mains :

Cannelloni :
An immaculately presented dish with spinach Cannelloni served with Salsa Rosa . This a definite must to enjoy delicacy of the outlet .

Lasagna :
Again a super delicious dish straight from the treasure box of chef special delicacy of the outlet .

Mocktails :

We went for our all time favourite classic Mocktails during our visit . Mojito ,  Shikanji and Blue Curacao were amongst the Favourites .

Dessert:

Tiramisu :
After a very long time we really enjoyed our most beloved dessert at this super cool place .

Zucotto :
Now that's a dessert for which we will visit the place soon again . Just don't miss on this the moment you are going for dessert out here . Outer coating of chocolate Creamy pastry stuffed with freezing cold icecream and fruits .

Do visit the Italian  Food Fiesta  at Le Bar Diamantaire  Sofitel  before 21st  June  2018 to have a great experience as we did.

For starters, we tried the Veg Shikampuri, Palak Patta Chaat, and Chur Chur Paneer, all of which were absolutely superb in taste and presentation. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner}, time_line=a month ago, review=⭐ 1/5
Extremely Disappointed with the Food Quality

I’m genuinely shocked by today’s experience at Malhaar Restaurant.

I had ordered from Zomato , the Veg Kofta was utterly bizarre and it had tutti frutti and cherries in it! Who puts dessert ingredients in a savoury kofta? It felt to me like the chef got confused between making a sweet dish and a main course. I paid ~₹450 for what tasted like a bland, uninspired dessert -definitely not a proper kofta!

The Hyderabadi Chicken too was devoid of flavour, lacking any authentic taste or spice balance. Overall, both dishes were pathetic and not worth the money.

What’s even more disappointing is that this isn’t the first time the quality has dropped. During our previous visit last month, the Manchow Soup we ordered was also far below expectations : watery, poorly seasoned, and lacking the usual flavour punch we associate with Malhaar. The soup wasn't simmered properly.

We’ve been regular customers and always appreciated the food before, but after today’s experience, I’m seriously skeptical about ever ordering from Malhaar again., name_person=Laxmi Patel}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=This place is heaven for South Indian seafood lovers! Ambience - The place has transformed from a shady bar to a classy place with great ambience. The new colors give a very happy feeling to the place.
Food - I have been going to the place for the past 10 years, even before writing reviews was not a thing. Frankly the restaurant was not that impressive but in the past year they have undergone a major reform and ohh boy they nailed it! Malhaar has entered the scene as a sea food specialist and with a bang. The food is simply great! We were served by the Shrimp Man, who has been working at the place for 16 years now. I would suggest to go with what he suggests as the menu is pretty diverse with a lot of cuisines.
Service - They have a good staff and service will be quick with the food. The bar service is slow for the cocktails so order well in advance for the next round.
Recommendation - I am a hardcore non vegetarian and a sea food lover. The picks of the day were 1. The crab meat soup 🌶. 2. Assorted ravas fry. (Would suggest to go for the surmai instead) 3. Prawns fry in barbeque sauce. 4. Prawns ghee roast with Neer Dosa.

We asked the Sikh Manager present there for suggestions in starters section and he was spot on with them
He served us with Prawns Naked Fry which was really good with prawns tossed in Chilli Paste with a hint of lime and curry leaves.
Next he suggested was Pepper Chicken Fry which I thought would be dry chicken which is the way it is prepared traditionally but rather they were small Chunks of chicken cut and coated with Batter and then fried with green chillies and curry leaves. It was a unique dish and was really tasty.

Next we tried some chicken slice with had very light Green Chilli batter and the chicken was succulent and really soft. It was the cherry on top.

We ordered Prawns Malvani Biryani for main course and Butter Naan and Chicken Birista.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservation required, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=1. Location & ambience
•	Gallops is located inside the Mahalaxmi Race Course in Mumbai, which gives it a uniquely lush, open-green backdrop uncommon in the city’s dining scene.  ￼
•	The décor and setting combine colonial charm with upscale comfort: for example, walnut-floors, candle-light chandeliers, and equestrian-themed décor post-revamp.  ￼
•	Outdoor and al-fresco dining is one of its strong suits — especially nice in cooler months.  ￼

2. Food quality & menu variety
•	The menu successfully blends Indian and Continental dishes. From traditional kebabs and curries to refined European-style mains, there’s something for varied tastes.  ￼
•	Signature dishes that get strong mentions:
•	“Dori Kebab” (mutton or chicken) – minced, skewered and charcoal-cooked.  ￼
•	“Chicken Ala Kiev” with cheese/butter-filled centre, as a refined European choice.  ￼
•	Desserts are also strong: Baked Alaska and newer additions like Baileys Caramel Cloud.  ￼
•	Many reviewers emphasize the generous portions, good presentation and a sense of value for a fine-dining venue.  ￼

3. Service & experience
•	The service is frequently praised: attentive staff, good recommendations (e.g., for wine or pairings), smooth reservation experience when booked in advance.  ￼
•	The overall dining experience is described as memorable— especially when everything aligns (good table, nice view, well-timed service). For example:
“What a wonderful restaurant from the minute we arrived the staff were so efficient and helpful, the food was absolutely incredible.”  ￼

4. Ideal for special occasions / date nights
•	The ambience, décor and location make it ideal for anniversaries, special dinners or when you want to treat yourself. Many mentions of formative visits, nostalgic moments, photo-friendly setting.  ￼

If I were picking one restaurant for a refined Mumbai meal — especially if you’re after something more than just dinner but an experience — Gallops checks a lot of boxes:
•	A setting that feels premium yet relaxed.
•	A menu that offers both familiar Indian comfort and elevated Continental touches.
•	Good enough service to let you focus on the evening rather than logistics.
•	A chance to dine in one of Mumbai’s less-hustle zones (given the race-course setting) while still being accessible.

If you ask me: go for the outdoor or window-view table (book ahead), order one of the signature starters + a main you haven’t tried, and finish with one of the classic desserts. ["{guided_block={}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=I visited Bayroute and honestly, the food and drinks were such a refreshing experience.
The Lemon Mint was the perfect thirst-quencher with its strong lemon flavour and fresh mint.
The Thai Meets Middle East drink was so unique coconut water, forest honey and herbs blended beautifully.
Their Hummus Bayroute was super creamy, and the labneh with zaatar and pine nuts made it even better.
I loved the Chicken Afrikaan which was spicy, flavourful and perfectly grilled with that hint of cumin.
The Kebab Istanbul was a melt-in-the-mouth mutton seekh kebab that tasted amazing.
Even the prawns were delicious, cooked in a tangy tomato gravy that balanced the flavours well.
And to end the meal, the Baklava with gulkand ice cream was just heavenly.
Crispy layers, nuts, rose brittles everything came together perfectly.
Overall, it was a wholesome, flavourful meal that felt special from start to finish.
Would definitely go back again!, name_person=Tanishka Chavan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Bayroute BKC never disappoints — but this time, they’ve truly outdone themselves with their Kebab & Meze Festival. The moment you step in, the ambience wraps you in warm golden lights and Mediterranean charm — it’s luxe yet cozy, elegant yet soulful.

I started my meal with the Ruyhan, a bright orange cooler that’s refreshing and slightly citrusy — the perfect start to a rich Middle Eastern feast. Their Zaffrani Chai was another star — aromatic, creamy, and comforting, with just the right hint of saffron.

Only went for the Bao, and they were good., name_person=kevin saji}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Salad], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=a year ago, review=Linking Road in Bandra is home to some of the best food in the city, and one of the best asian joints in the place is The fatty Bao. It has a modern, chic vibe crossed with a vibrant and sassy decor, perfect for a date night, or for a hangout sesh with friends.

The decor feels inspired by Malay/Singaporean cafes, with a lot of the artwork depicting the same, and it comes off pretty well. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, though the indoor seating is a bit cramped, but that's mostly fine. They do have a small bar serving the usual suspects, as well as some of their own stuff.

While I didn't get to order a large chunk of their menu, whatever I had was pretty great. Their name is definitely apt, as the baos I got were plump and pillowy, and the filling was perfect. I got the pork char siu baos, and the pork was fatty and melt in your mouth, complimented nicely by a slice of raw apple, giving it a fruity kick. Every Bao order comes with two, making it perfect for date night.

I also got their raw papaya salad, which was one of the best renditions of the dish I've eaten in Mumbai. It was tangy, sweet and spicy in just the right amounts, and wasn't just a refreshing palate cleanser, but a great meal by itself. It's also a very generous portion making it great for sharing.

The last thing I got were Chicken and asparagus dumplings, which didn't impress me as much, as I've had better dumplings in the same price range. They weren't bad but not particularly great either. The filling was generous, but it lacked in flavor. For 6 pieces, it was not the best value, and I recommend trying other dumplings, or avoiding dumplings all together.

Overall, I would rate both the Char Siu Bao and the Papaya Salad a solid 9/10, and the dumplings about a 6.5/10. Definitely go for their baos( pretty obvious given their name).

The service was fine, but they do tend to ignore the smaller tables and focus on the bigger groups, and it was also pretty busy on the day I visited. But I did see other tables also not receiving food at the proper times, so I'd rate the service a little lower, like a 6/10. Definitely could do with some improvement.

The Fatty Bao definitely ticks a lot of the boxes, though they do miss a little bit in their service, and cocktail variety, though I did not have the opportunity to try it. However, they more than make up for it with their snazzy decor and contemporary vibe, along with some pretty great food. I highly recommend checking the place out if you're out shopping in Linking Road and need to grab some lunch or dinner. You're definitely gonna be leaving a happy and fatty bao when you're done.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=A school friend sent me a reel about Poe and Pao in Chembur. I decided to go chasing Poe and Pao. Since I was already in Bandra, I thought I’d try their Matunga outlet instead.

Now, if you’re a true-blue Mumbaikar, you know traffic jams aren’t an inconvenience, they’re a lifestyle. So there I was, stuck in the middle of one, wishing for a restroom more than anything else.

When I finally reached, they said, “Go next door.” I stumbled into Dakshin Culture Curry and found the cleanest restroom in Mumbai. Small, but spotless. You can’t do pranayama there, but you’ll definitely come out feeling zen.

Feeling human again, I stepped out… and somehow found myself in Diva Maharashtracha. For a moment, I thought I’d taken a wrong turn in life. That’s when someone explained that Dakshin Culture Curry, Goa Portuguesa, and Diva Maharashtracha are a trilogy, same team, shared menu, different cuisines. And Poe and Pao? The latest addition to the family.

One look at the menu, and I knew there was no way I was walking back to Poe and Pao.

I started with a Sushegad Shot (feni, lime, and kaffir leaves) -  Goa in a glass. Then came the Khekade Kalimiri Soup, a crab-and-black-pepper combo that doubles as a natural sinus reliever. After that, Ravas Moile, Tender Coconut Cashew Nut Sukke (their signature dish), Chicken Modak, and Appam n Amboli.

The Chicken Modak was the surprise star—moist chicken kheema wrapped in a soft, pillowy coating. Though, between us, it did look slightly jaundiced.

They ended the meal with complimentary Caramel Custard—light, soft, and just the right sweetness.

The staff were courteous and attentive, the ambience warm and welcoming.

Ambience: A+
Food: A+++

In Starters 🍢
🔸Fish Fry Porichaphu 🐟❤️
This was a very tempting dish. Pomphret which was nicely marinated was served in red masala and fried. It had a nice tangy sweet taste. The covering was crisp with hint of spices and the sauce served along was tangy sweet. A must try!

Rawas fish marinated with spices and yogurt and nicely grilled. The flavors were soaked in the fish. The dish was so well prepared that all I wanted to eat was this yummy Rawas. My new favorite.

🔸Cosmopolitan 🍸❤️💯
Our usual favorite. This Cocktail was well prepared. Just the way I like it. Nothing can ever go wrong with Cosmo. Went perfectly well with the starters.

This was tangy sweet due to the mango flavor but again a yummy boozy drink. Well served with sugar coated at the rim. It was an eye candy.

🔸Prawns Manglorean Sukkha 🍤❤️💯
This was a delight. If you want something light to go with your breads then this is it. This was so flavorful and tasty. Hint of all the spices nicely marinated in prawns. The prawns were in good number and juicy.

This was the best Chicken Chettinad. Spicy and tasty, with so many flavors. I could eat it everyday. Just like homemade gravies but much more flavors and spices. Too yum. A must must try here.

🔸Malabar Paratha
It was served hot and crisp. Went really well with Chettinad gravy and the chicken pieces.

🔹Appam ❤️
They've a special counter to make appams. And my mum loved it to the core that through out the meal she had more of appams. Beautifully made and served steaming hot.

🔸Neer Dosa
Soft and light. Non sticky and thin slices. The beauty of neer dosa. Just perfect.

In Desserts 🍦
🔹Shahi Tukda ❤️
Fried bread stuffed with rabdi. The rabdi was so so good. Specially made by the chef. It was full of rich milky flavors.

Visited Urban Tadka in Mulund West expecting a rich North Indian dining experience, but sadly, the evening was filled with more misses than hits. The vibe and branding promise a lot—but the food didn’t live up to it.

⸻

🍗 Happy Chicken Tikka – Underdone & Flat

The chicken was quite raw inside, with spices that felt slapped on rather than blended in. Texture was off and flavor didn’t settle. Disappointing, especially for something that’s supposed to be a highlight.

⸻

🐟 Fish Tikka – The Only Redeemer

This was the best dish of the evening. Perfectly cooked, well spiced, flaky and hot. If only the rest of the meal had matched this level.

⸻

🌶️ Garlic Chutney – Always Great

Still one of their strengths—bold, spicy, and garlicky. Goes well with almost anything.

⸻

🫓 Masala Papad – Shockingly Bad

I’ve had good masala papad here in the past, but this time it was very poorly done—soggy in parts, unevenly topped, and clearly rushed. It was a huge letdown, especially for such a simple dish.

⸻

🍷 Sangria – Just Syrupy Sweetness

This wasn’t sangria—it tasted like fruit syrup mixed with soda. No wine flavour, no balance, and way too sweet. It felt like a mocktail trying to pass as something it’s not.

⸻

🍮 Jalebi & Rabadi – Uneven Again
•	Rabadi: Thick, creamy, and well-made. A small win at the end of the meal.
•	Jalebi: Absolutely terrible. Not only was it soggy and bland, but it had a strong chemical smell—almost like bleach, which was shocking and off-putting.

⸻

💬 Final Thoughts

Urban Tadka Mulund is clearly struggling with quality control. From raw chicken and bad jalebi to sloppy basics like masala papad, this meal felt rushed and careless. The fish tikka, garlic chutney, and rabadi were the only saving graces.

⸻

❌ Final Verdict

Not worth the hype or the price. When half the items are badly executed—and one smells like cleaning fluid—it’s a red flag.
Urban Tadka needs to seriously rework their kitchen consistency if they want to live up to their name.

Would not return in a hurry.

Kebab Corner:

A Chinese Twist:

Overall Experience:

🥂 Drinks
We started off with some refreshing mocktails:

Pandas Ale – Refreshing, unique, and a hit with my friend too.
Sa Bi Tonic – Very unique in flavor, and we absolutely loved it.
Hawaiian Colada – Not only delicious but beautifully presented as well.
🍢 Starters
Chicken Gyozas – Soft yet crunchy with a flavor we all enjoyed.
Chicken Yakitori – Unique and flavorful, a definite highlight.
Yuzu Tempura Prawns – Great taste and presentation; we were impressed.
🍕 Main Course
Our mains were recommended by the chef and did not disappoint:

Five Spice Chicken Pizza (Thin Crust) – A showstopper with incredible flavor that I, my friend, and my brother all loved.
Thai Basil Chicken – Bursting with flavor and absolutely mind-blowing.
🍮 Dessert

👨‍🍳 Service

He then asked if we were staying at the hotel and was shocked to hear that we were and then finally apologised for the bill. Very strange encounter. As we left he thanked is for highlighting the bill discrepancy and apologised. We believe we were overcharged on purpose. Unfortunately, this turned out to be one of the most underwhelming buffet dinners we’ve had in a long time.

To begin with, the vegetarian selection was extremely limited, which itself was disappointing for a premium luxury hotel. What made it worse was that several items had already run out by around 9:30–10 PM, which is surprisingly early for a dinner buffet. The veg sushi, in particular, was tucked away inside the refrigerator with no proper labelling or indication—it genuinely felt like a game of hide-and-seek unless you already knew where to look.

We were excited to try the chaat and gol gappas (puchkas), but this was hands down the worst part of the experience. The chaat was served cold, soggy, and overly sweet, even after we specifically requested mild spice. The gol gappas were shockingly plain—filled only with boondi and nothing else, completely missing the usual exciting mix of chutneys, potatoes, or flavours.

The Indian vegetarian main course was mediocre at best, lacking both variety and flavour. The only true highlight from the Indian section was the freshly made garlic naan, which was genuinely good. The hot dim sum station was another pleasant surprise, as those were freshly cooked and nicely done.

A special mention must be made of the pancake counter—the lady handling it was warm and sweet, and the fact that the pancakes were eggless won us over completely. Though pancakes aren’t a typical dinner or dessert item, this ended up being the most enjoyable part of our meal.

Service suffered due to severe understaffing. The staff, though polite, seemed unsure of menu details themselves, and the small dining arena with closly sat tables, which further affected the overall experience.

Overall, this dinner experience was a 5/10 at best. As Accor Gold members who genuinely love Accor properties, this was by far one of the most disappointing dining experiences we’ve had in recent times. I recently visited Pondicherry Café at Sofitel in Mumbai, and unfortunately, the experience fell far below expectations. Here’s a detailed breakdown of my visit:

Parking Hassle

As someone who arrived on a motorbike, the experience began with a significant disappointment. The hotel does not provide motorbike parking within its premises. Instead, I was directed to a pay-and-park lot 300 meters away, located on an open ground opposite Jio International School. This parking area was poorly maintained and inconvenient, especially for those with huge bikes like mine. I had to leave my bike without a handle locked, which was unsettling.

Walking from the parking lot to the hotel in the scorching sun further diminished the experience. For a luxury hotel, this lack of accommodation for bikers is surprising and disheartening.

Ambience and Atmosphere

Once inside, the ambience of Pondicherry Café was pleasant but lacked any accompanying music, which made it feel somewhat lifeless. The décor was appealing, but the overall atmosphere could use some warmth and vibrance to match the expectations of a premium dining experience.

Buffet Experience

We opted for the buffet based on its promising menu, but the food did not deliver in terms of taste. While there was a variety of options available, very few stood out. Here’s a breakdown of the meal:
•	Soup: 2/5 – Bland and unremarkable.
•	Starters: 3/5 – Only two items were decent; the rest were forgettable.
•	Main Course: 2/5 – A disappointing selection with subpar flavors.
•	Desserts: 2/5 – Average at best. The pista kulfi had an odd paan flavor, which didn’t appeal to me.
•	Pizza & Pasta: Possibly the worst I’ve ever had.

Overall, the food lacked flavor and quality, especially considering the premium pricing.

Service

The service was another letdown. Staff were hard to find when needed, whether it was for cutlery or water. This lack of attentiveness added to the frustration and further detracted from the overall dining experience.

Final Thoughts

For a restaurant within a luxury hotel, Pondicherry Café failed to meet expectations on multiple fronts. The motorbike parking issue, coupled with an underwhelming dining experience, made this visit quite disappointing. Considering the high ratings this restaurant holds on platforms like Zomato and Google, I feel it is overrated.

Recommendation:
•	For Bikers: Avoid this place if you value convenience and proper parking facilities.
•	For Food Lovers: There are far better dining options in the BKC area offering superior taste, service, and overall experience at similar or lower price points.

Overall Rating:
•	Ambience: 3/5
•	Food Taste: 2/5
•	Service: 2/5
•	Value for Money: 1/5

["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Today had visited here with family for Dinner. This is located in Borivali West. Ample parking is available. The ambience is excellent. Sitting is very spacious and comfortable.

The ambiance of the place was perfect for spending quality time with loved ones - cozy and comfortable. The restaurant had a warm and inviting feel to it, and I immediately felt at home.

We started off with some refreshing mocktails - the Pink Panther, made with guava and chili, and the Fruit Punch. Both were absolutely delicious and really hit the spot. For starters, we ordered the Kun Pao Paneer and the Mozzarella Hariyali Tikki. The Kun Pao Paneer was spicy and flavorful, while the Hariyali Tikki was a delightful mix of mozzarella and herbs.

Moving on to the main course, we had the Paneer Butter Masala and the Manchurian Noodles. The Paneer Butter Masala was rich and creamy, and the Manchurian Noodles were perfectly cooked with just the right amount of spice.

For dessert, we had the Vanilla Ice Cream and the Raj Bhog Ice Cream. Both were amazing and the perfect end to our meal.

Overall, I would highly recommend Lotus Leaf Cafe to anyone looking for a cozy and inviting atmosphere, great food, and excellent service. reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Been here few days back for lunch. This restaurant is cited inside a 4 star property i.e Ramee Guestline Dadar.

Rasoi kitchen and bar is all about the experience and top notch f&b.
The entire restaurant is well designed which has this really nice and calming Atmosphere and it looks fab. Loved the decor a lot as there are few elements which looks quirky and premium.

So we had a couple of drinks and food dishes over here and we loved every single thing.
For drinks we ordered for Anar ka pyar which was mix of pomegranate, cranberry and lime juice. Loved it! Also from the mango special menu we tried Mango Colada which was hands down the best one in my opinion and we would strongly recommend trying this one.

For Starters they have a lot to choose from. We ordered Prawns sukka which was this semi thick gravy having the dominant flavor of Coconut and home ground spices. Fabulous!
Also had Murgh Multani Tikka which was by far one of the best kebab we have tasted. First up the portion served was twice what we get anywhere. Loved the plating too!

Later for the main course we had Prawns Goan curry which was scrumptious and had perfect consistency. 5 pieces of decent sized prawns into that luscious gravy paired with naan was true bliss. Last up we had Thai curry which was served with steamed rice and it had a good amount of veggies and chicken in it. Totally value for money and incredible taste as well.

Desserts are always my favourite part of the meal and rasoi made sure we had a great ending for this yummy meal. In house Kulfi Falooda was our call and right from the presentation to taste it was lovely. If you are someone who loves falooda then this one for you.

Rasoi kitchen & Bar offers really nice service as well. The staff is well trained and they are quite attentive too. Would be visiting here again with my family., name_person=V&S}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=As I entered Rasoi, I was greeted by a warm and inviting ambiance with elegant decor and comfortable seating. The attentive staff promptly escorted me to my table, and I was eager to explore the menu. I started my culinary journey with their Mocktail Caribbean Delight, a refreshing blend of tropical fruit flavors with a hint of mint, which was a perfect start to my meal. My companion opted for the cocktail New York Sour, a classic whiskey-based cocktail with a tangy twist of lemon, which was a perfect balance of sweet and sour notes.

For appetizers, we tried the Murg Mastani Tikka and Bhatti da Murg. The Murg Mastani Tikka was a succulent and flavorful chicken tikka marinated with aromatic spices, while the Bhatti da Murg was a juicy and tender tandoori chicken with a smoky flavor that left us craving for more. The combination of the two appetizers was a perfect blend of traditional and contemporary flavors, and we thoroughly enjoyed them.

Moving on to the main course, we opted for the Nawabi Murg with Cheese Garlic Naan and Nukkad Wali Biryani. The Nawabi Murg was a rich and creamy chicken curry with a velvety gravy that was packed with flavors. The chicken was cooked to perfection, and the dish was a perfect balance of spices and creaminess. The Cheese Garlic Naan was a heavenly combination of gooey cheese and aromatic garlic, which complemented the curry perfectly. The Nukkad Wali Biryani was a fragrant and flavorful rice dish with tender pieces of meat and aromatic spices that were a treat to the taste buds.

To end our culinary journey on a sweet note, we indulged in the Kulfi Falooda, a classic Indian dessert with a twist. The creamy and rich kulfi was served with a generous topping of vermicelli and rose syrup, which added a burst of flavors to the dessert. The service at Rasoi was impeccable, with attentive staff who were knowledgeable about the menu and provided prompt service throughout our meal. Calcutta, Andheri – A True Bengali Feast in Mumbai

I dropped by Oh! Calcutta in Andheri for a late lunch, and honestly, it was one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in a while.

The restaurant is easy to find—right on the highway—and the vibe hits you as soon as you walk in. It’s warm, inviting, and has that polished-but-comfortable feel. When I was seated, I noticed these gorgeous white plates with vintage Bengali prints—they looked stunning and added a nice touch to the setting. Next came the Gondhoraj Shorbot, made with a special lemon sourced from Bengal. The waiter recommended it, and I’m glad I listened. Refreshing, light, and a total palate cleanser. A hidden gem.

Then came the heavy hitters: Calcutta Mutton Biryani and Mutton Kosha. I’d always wanted to try their Kosha, but usually with luchi. It’s not your typical masala-heavy biryani—it’s an acquired taste, but one I’ve come to love thanks to my Bengali friends over the years.

For dessert, I went with the Baked Rosogolla—another hit. The portion was smaller than expected, but it packed a punch. Baked with rabdi, it was warm, comforting, and a perfect end to the meal. Oh, and they even offered a complimentary paan on the way out. Nice touch.

But despite the charming name and the promise of a thoughtfully curated Italian menu, the experience left more to be desired than remembered.

The meal started on a reasonably positive note. The Spaghetti Carbonara arrived with a creamy, well-emulsified sauce that clung nicely to the strands of pasta. The presence of pork gave the dish some much-needed body and savouriness, though it was hard to tell if guanciale was used. The overall flavour was pleasant, if unremarkable, and the dish did what it needed to without dazzling.

Unfortunately, the meal only declined from there.

The Steak, requested medium rare, did arrive at the correct doneness, which deserves acknowledgement. But that’s where the positives end. The cut of meat itself was a poor choice—tough, chewy, and devoid of the tenderness one expects from a properly sourced and rested steak. For a dish that typically commands a premium on any menu, this one felt more like an afterthought than a main event.

The Salmon Bruschetta fared no better. Topped with pallid, clearly farmed salmon that lacked freshness, the dish suffered from a lack of depth and definition. The cream which is meant to support or complement actually ended up dominating the plate. The result was a bland, vaguely fishy bite that could have come from any cold appetiser counter rather than a kitchen claiming Italian sophistication.

And therein lies the central issue with Napoli by Shatranj. While it gestures toward authenticity and finesse, the food rarely lands with the kind of precision or character that might distinguish it. The pricing, meanwhile, reflects a confidence that the food does not back up. At best, it feels like another stylish Bandra restaurant with a name borrowed from Naples but very little of its soul.
