All in all, for veg Options are limited and not worth paying so much for., name_person=Sachi Gandhhi}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Illuminati

“Beautiful things and Delicious food is priceless.” It’s a thought come to my mind when I’ve visited newly opened place in BKC named Illuminati. This place surprises me in my first visit. As you entered the place, it’s a different world altogether.

This place certainly raises the bar chicness and opulence. With all positive vibes and great hospitality Illuminati won accolades.

The place lit with beautiful white lights, classy décor and huge bar. They have a wide collection of Alcohol and wines.

The amazing indulgence of spices and the flavors has made me their fan. The varied menu has really tempted my taste buds and taken it to a niche.

So, first let’s start with cocktails and then food.

Prisoner: Vodka based (kettle one) with Galangal and Lemongrass. Loved the freshness and sweet taste because of lemongrass.

Blue Fairy: Jim Beam + Blueberry + Blue Pea Bitters + Orange slice. Looks amazing but tasted less of alcohol. Maybe not stirred well, still can give a try.

Believer: Believe me, it’s the best one among all three. Kettle One Vodka+ Chamomile spiced Apple + Thyme. Really amazing. This was smooth, fresh and bit different.

Quick Steamed Rawas Xiao Xing: Loved the balance. Bold flavors. Very smooth texture. Presentation is beautiful. Rawas fish is served with Xiao Xing wine. Overall colourful and made well. Do try.

Tokyo Chicken Karrage: This looks amazing and tasted so good, crunchy. You can taste both sweet and spicy at the same time. I could actually feel the distinct flavors yet intact.

Tempura Prawn: It delectably delights you. One of the best tempura prawn sushi I had in recent time. Tasted lovely.

Chicken and Bok Choy: It was simply great. Bok Choi is a type of Chinse Cabbage. Minced Chicken and Bok Choy has a generous stuffing. Served hot. Do try.

Honey Sesame Chicken Bowl: I still cannot get over this. The star dish of the day. Diced chicken tossed in sticky sesame soy with a bit of 5 pickled chillies. All the herbs intact and served with Jasmine rice was a delicious treat to my gluttony.

The Decadent Cake French Toast: Not too sweet. But not to be miss for sure.

Time and again I would just sing praises for this absolutely amazing place which makes sure to lure its patron and woo them with delicious offerings.

P.S: The review is strictly depending on my personal experience.

["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Thane Pub Exchange is the perfect Friday night fun place for you and yours friends to unwind! Listen to music and show some moves on that amazing dance floor of theirs or even watch your favorite Cricket match! For ordering drinks, they have a special app which you can easily download from the play store! The prices for the drinks fluctuate just like a stock exchange (hence the name) and you can choose to order your drinks accordingly! The ambience is very cool and the seating is quite comfortable. The service is a tad bit slow but the food made up for it nonetheless! Coming to the food we had...

1.Classic Paneer Tikka(5/5)
The paneer was oh-so-soft and the marination was perfect! The salad and chutney went along perfectly well!

2.Paneer Chilli Milli(5/5)
The classic paneer chilli! The paneer was soft and melted in your mouth! The sauce was perfect, spicy and tangy!

3.Chocolate Brownie with Icecream (5/5)
One of the best brownies I've ever had! The brownie was super duper fresh and soft! The Icecream went with it quite well!

Overall a good experience! Keep up the great food.  Will surely visit again soon! ;), name_person=Purva Mundlye}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Thane Pub Exchange is a Bar & Lounge launched by Smaaash in Korum Mall is just a perfect place to chill, hangout with friends & family with food, games and lots of fun I can say its an Extra ordinary place to spend your holiday having some creative experiences.

Talking about Thane pub Exchange bar has an expansive seating space with wooden flooring. The bar is exquisitely decorated with inverted glasses and offers a wide selection of spirits. They have both indoor and outdoor mall seating arrangement. Thane pub Exchange has both veg and non-veg options. The food menu is primarily continental and Indian. A Pair of Mocktail or cocktail with mouthwatering cheesy Munchies like Classic Nachos, smash Basket etc will be perfect along with mains can go for freshly baked pizza’s, veg chopper Bowl, pasta bowl is equally delicious. The have pocket friendly buffet & beer plus games for kids, adults on Sundays.

The ambience is vibrant and classic with live music ample of space for dance, huge screening of the matches it’s a total relaxing environment to pamper yourself.

I personally was overjoyed being at this wonderful place. The crowd too is very lively and enjoying. I had called for Kokum Buster an outstanding mocktail with right amount of fizz and tanginess it was so refreshing, and chilled prepared right must try. Bull Ride was great combination of Orange juice with red bull revitalizing one made with crushed ice trilling experience having it.

Fish N Chips

Juicy chicken tossed in creamy coconut garlic based sauce tasted delicious. Loved the flavours in this as even this had coconut milk it wasn’t sweet and the chicken was tender.

Chicken Shole -
One of the best classic chicken tikka experiences as this dish tasted outstanding. Spice rub was really food, the grilling was perfect and the chutney onion served along was great.

MAINS~
Paneer Tikka Pizza -
Nicely done base topped with sauce, cheese and paneer tikka tasted good. It was a classic pizza done right.

Chicken Korean Rice -
Looked delicious and tasted exactly the same. Basic yet full marks for this as the rice done in Korean sauce along with egg and chicken tasted great.

DESSERT~
Chocolate Brownie -
Fresh chocolate brownie topped with chocolate sauce and ice cream was a perfect end.

BEVERAGES~
Love Dream.
Malta Basil.
Both the drinks tasted good and went well with the food.

Peach Iced Tea is a refreshing burst of flavor in every sip.

Kalimiri Cheddar Broccoli
From the moment the dish arrives, the vibrant green of the broccoli is contrasted beautifully by the creamy richness of the cheddar cheese, infused with the subtle yet captivating warmth of kalimiri (black pepper). The aroma is inviting—cheesy, slightly spicy, and earthy.The broccoli retains a nice crunch, providing a fresh, earthy base to the dish. The cheddar is indulgently smooth, delivering a familiar, comforting creaminess. But what sets this dish apart is the kalimiri. The black pepper’s spice gently lingers, balancing the richness of the cheese with a subtle heat. The tender yet slightly crisp broccoli pairs wonderfully with the velvety melted cheddar. Perfect for those looking for something familiar with a hint of spice. However, the spice of cardamom was overpowered and sat on tongue, so every bite was full of cardamom, which made the next dishes taste like it too.

Tiranga Kofte
Visually, the Tiranga Kofte presents itself well, with three distinct layers symbolizing the colours of the Indian flag. The presentation is appealing and sets high expectations for a flavourful experience. However, the dish's appearance slightly outweighs its taste. The kofte has a decent blend of spices, though the flavours don’t quite come together as cohesively as expected. Each layer brings something different—the green layer offers a mild herbiness, the white layer is a bit bland, and the orange section has a touch of heat. However, the balance between them feels uneven, with the spices not blending as harmoniously as they should.
Since the appetizer had cardamom hint which was overpowering, the outer layer green part of kofta also felt it had cardamom which wasn’t pleasant on tongue.

Jeera rice

Halwa (Complementary)

["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Barrel Mansion

Barrel Mansion is the new talk of the town. This is a club with a great ambiance, quick service and amazing food, really I just loved this place. This place is open till 3.00 am. Located within the Sahara Star hotel in Vile Parle East Mumbai.

The ambience of this place is certainly the best part of the place. It gives us these crazy vibes as soon as we enter. I visited here few days ago and enjoyed my time.

We started with Som Tam Salad had the punch. Dressing was perfect. Bang on flavors. Raw papaya in a traditional sour and spicy marinade. One of the best salads I have tried in recent time.

Dynamite Prawns: Medium sized battered prawns served in a margarita glass made in chef special sauce. Prawns has an amazing texture and was delicious. The topping of black and white sesame was icing on the cake. Loved this one.

Stir Fry Chicken: Chicken chunks and fresh exotic veggies tossed in sauce and spices. You can feel sweet and spicy taste at a same time.

Prawns Crackers: One of the best option to nibble with a drink.

Black Bean Sauce Chicken: Loved the punch of pepper in it. Goes very well Chicken Fried Rice. Combination is superb. Black Bean Sauce was more on spicier side. But, still go for it.

Sesame Ice Cream: Its creamy hand churned icecream made in-house and topped with black sesame

Tab Tim Grob: Not so good for me. The presentation was good but tasted okayish.

Overall, Loved the ambience, service and food. Keep up the good work. Cheers!!!

Food: 5/5

Service: 5/5

Ambience: 5/5

USP :- Decent Decor, Lively Ambience, Live DJ, Delicious Food, Signature Cocktails @ reasonable prices

DECOR, AMBIENCE & SEATING

They have a full fledged bar which offers a wide variety of mocktails & signature cocktails to spoil you for choices.
The place offers indoor seating only which is compact in size, seating is well spaced out & comfortable.
The Bar is located in one corner, seating is spread in the middle while the DJ plays some peppy tracks on his console from the other end.
They have two large tv screens on both sides to enjoy live sports while you munch on tasty food & sip classic cocktails 🍸

OUR FOOD & DRINK ORDER

Veg Starters
* Stuffed Tandoori Aloo Nazakat
* Paneer kalimirch
* Crispy chilli lime potato
* Salted baby corn mushrooms broccoli
* Veg spring roll

Main Course
A) Indian main course
* Punjabi chana masala

B) Chinese main course
* Thai bamboo rice

DRINKS
Mocktail
Water Melon cooler

Cocktails
Guava Mary hai
Kafir orange blast
Downtown sangria
Downtown sour
Bull frog

FOOD & DRINKS REVIEW

Their Food delivers on all fronts in terms of quality, quantity, taste & presentation.

Their Signature cocktails are made using unique combinations, decent alcohol level & less ice which balances the drink perfectly (not too light or strong).

STAFF & PRICING
The Staff is well groomed, polite, attentive & well rehearsed with the menu to make you comfortable & your food experience delightful.

In terms of pricing this place scores really well as their prices are reasonable when you account for the food & drink portions served.

A great place to catch up with family and friends where you can munch on tasty food, sip on drinks while dancing on foot tapping numbers and having a blast without burning a hole in your pocket., name_person=Akshay Davda}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=36 Downtown is a new outlet located within walking distance from the Grant Road Station. Chang’s at Lower Parel is one of those places you walk into with a certain set of expectations — especially for dinner. Big space, familiar menu, and that promise of bold Asian flavours. Our visit was mostly enjoyable, but a few things definitely held it back from being a great meal.

Let’s start with the biggest issue of the night — temperature. A surprising number of dishes arrived almost cold. Not “could be hotter” warm, but genuinely needing to be sent back. We had to request reheating more than once, which took away from the flow of the meal. For a restaurant of this scale and reputation, that was disappointing and honestly shouldn’t happen.

Drinks came first. The Samurai Fizz (2.5/5) was… fine. Refreshing, yes, but pretty forgettable. It didn’t really stand out in flavour. On the other hand, the Passionfruit Iced Tea (4.5/5) was excellent — well-balanced, refreshing, and easily the best drink we ordered.

Soups were a letdown. Both the Hot & Sour Soup (2/5) and Chang’s Noodle Soup (2/5) lacked depth and warmth — in flavour and temperature. They felt rushed and flat, which is a shame because these are usually comforting starters.

Things picked up once the appetisers started rolling in. The Shrimp Tempura Roll (4/5) was nicely done — crispy shrimp, clean flavours, and well-balanced textures. The Pan Fried Handmade Shrimp Dumplings (2/5), however, were underwhelming. Soft, yes, but bland and missing that punch you expect from dumplings.

Vegetarian dishes did surprisingly well. The Kung Pao Potatoes (4/5) were addictive — crispy, spicy, and full of flavour. Easily one of the better plates on the table.

Among the chicken dishes, both the Orange Chicken (4/5) and Dynamite Chicken (4/5) delivered what you expect — crispy, saucy, and comforting. No complaints there. But the real star of the night was the Ring of Fire Shrimp (5/5). Perfectly crispy, bold flavours, and just the right amount of heat. This dish alone made the wait and reheating worth it.

The Mongolian Tenderloin (3/5) was a mixed experience. The meat was beautifully tender, cooked just right, but the flavour was surprisingly bland. It needed more sauce or seasoning to really shine.

For sides, the Hong Kong Egg Fried Rice (4/5) was simple and satisfying, and the Chicken in Black Bean (4/5) was solid — comforting, flavourful, and reliable.

Desserts wrapped things up nicely. The Great Wall of Chocolate (4/5) was rich and indulgent without being too heavy, while the Banana Spring Roll (4/5) was crisp, warm, and a crowd-pleaser.

They genuinely tried to make the experience better, which made a big difference. The atmosphere was pleasant — lively but not chaotic — making it a comfortable place for a dinner outing.

Overall, P.F. Chang’s Lower Parel had some strong dishes and excellent service, but the repeated issue of food being served cold brought the overall experience down. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Shahi_Tukda], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=We visited Kebab Korner in intercontinental located at marine drive, a legacy restaurant started since 1980!

A true royal dining experience at Kebab Korner located inside intercontinental at Marine drive!

The staff is affable. I loved the food here. Very tasty and fresh. This place is located on 1st floor at intercontinental, Marine drive. They have lots of variety for kebab and north Indian food. The place is well maintained and neat. Ambience is royal. The best part is you get amazing Sea view while eating.

Food we called for was:-

Veg kebab platter (5/5)- This platter included broccoli marinated in mustard sauce, paneer Khali aaloo, veg seekh, jaitui paneer. We loved this one.

Daal makhani (5/5)- Amazingly cooked. A must order dish here.

Lacha chur(55/)- it's crushed paratha with red chilli as garnishment.

Valet is available., name_person=saloni shah}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Kebab Korner is a restaurant with beautiful blue and white interiors along with artistic chairs which gives it a very royal look. To top it all this place has an amazing view of Mumbai’s Queen’s Necklace. It looks stunning, especially during the Monsoon Season.

The Cuisine here is Indian and they specialize in Kebabs and North Indian Curries. I have tried a lot of Vegetarian dishes here, which is mentioned in detail below.

Truffled Mushroom Baby Kulcha

Small Soft Kulchas Stuffed with a Mushroom Paste. It comes straight out of the tandoor to your plate! It was very soft when I tried it and it had a very mild flavor from the Mushrooms. However, I couldn't taste truffle anywhere, I was expecting the use of some truffle oil at least.

Chili Cheese Baby Kulcha

Another version of Soft Kulchas Stuffed with Cheese and lots of Red Chili Powder, I could taste a lot of cheese and the spice from the Red Chili was also not overpowering. I would prefer this over the Mushroom kulcha even though I LOVE Mushrooms.

Jaituni Paneer Tikka

Giant Cubes of Paneer Marinated in Tandoori Marinate and it was sliced from between to stuff in some Olives. That gave it a tangy flavor and it was an amazing way of serving the Paneer Tikka. The only thing I didn't like is the quantity of Olives was very less and I could hardly taste any Olives.

Kumbh Dak Banglow

Button Mushrooms marinated in a Mustard Paste and cooked inside the tandoor until they become soft.

Daal Makhani

A bowl full of richness, it was exactly what you expect from a Daal Makhani. Melt in mouth Daal in tonne loads of Butter & Cream with superb flavors coming from spices like Clove, Cumin and Cardamom.

Lehsooni Palak

A very creamy concoction of Spinach and Fried Garlic, this was hands down the best dish which I had here. It is a must try if you love Spinach.

The service here was very quick and the staff had total knowledge about the Menu. Overall this place was amazing and I would definitely recommend it to someone who loves to have North Indian Food., name_person=Paras}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=InterContinental - the iconic Hotel located at Marine Drive is home to Kebab Korner. Kebab Korner is an ultra luxurious fine dine place with breathtaking bayview and serves authentic Indian cuisine along with some fusion dishes / desserts as well. Kebab Korner is located on Level 1 alongside Long & Short, which is a lounge which serves European cuisine.

Kebab Korner has recently introduced Thalis - which is a lavish 3 course Indian meal including appetizers, main course and desserts. They offer Express Lunch Thali which caters to corporate as well and is priced at INR 1800 excluding wine. For dinner they offer "Experience Thali" which is an easy going complete meal, where you can take your time and enjoy scrumptious meal. This is priced at INR 2400.

Heading straight to what was on offer for Experience Thali - Veg

To begin with we were presented with a palate cleanser - Amuse Bouche. Crispy and Spiced Masala Chana Dal packed in edible plastic. I was intrigued about the ingredients used and technique to make this, but it stays as a secret with the restaurant and chef. Very unique and impressed I must say!

We started with Appetizers and were served three of them - Jaipuri Paneer Tikka, Bhune Subz Ki Shami and Sarson Brocolli Tandoori. Paneer Tikka was smoked cottage cheese marinated with olives. Toasted Almonds & Olives were on the house and were refilled even before we hit the bottom of the bowl.
We ordered
1. Smokey Kokey (Pineapple based, smoked cocktail) - Was very good, not too pineapple-y(sweet)
2. Berry Spritz - Not bad, but a regular Apperol Spritz of Lemon Spritz would've been nicer
3. Toadstool (Stuffed mushrooms) Good

Coming to the food, we tried the drunken noodles, veg SoBo fried rice, veg cheesy dimsums, and veg crackling sushi. The dimsums were the star of the meal, super soft, cheesy, and just the right kind of indulgent. Honestly, I’d go back just for them.

It's the kind of place you visit when you crave authentic, home-style seafood and fiery curries.
The highlight here is, without a doubt, the seafood. The fish is always incredibly fresh—a mandatory requirement for any great coastal establishment. I highly recommend starting with the Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck) or the Surmai Fry. The coating is perfectly crisp, and the marinade is a flawless blend of chili, turmeric, and spice. For the main course, the Prawn Curry Thali is a masterpiece; rich, coconut-based gravy that pairs perfectly with the soft, fluffy Vade (puri made from rice and lentil flour). If you prefer meat, the Chicken Malvani Thali is equally robust and satisfying.
Beyond the main courses, don't miss out on the incredible Solkadhi. This kokam-based digestive drink is creamy, tangy, and absolutely essential for cooling the palate after the spicy Konkani flavors. It’s one of the best I've had outside of a Konkani home.
The ambiance is simple, clean, and unpretentious, allowing the focus to remain solely on the food, as it should be. The staff is warm, helpful, and eager to offer recommendations, making the entire dining experience feel incredibly homely. If you love coastal flavors, fresh fish, and authentic Malvani spices, Konkan Swad is a must-visit destination in Jogeshwari. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=7 months ago, review=Extremely Disappointed with Service and Food Quality at Chulha Restobar – Not Recommended

Hi, I'm Khushbu Arora from KhushbuSaysItAll on Instagram. I generally share honest food experiences across platforms, and unfortunately, I had two very disappointing experiences with Chulha Restobar that I feel other customers deserve to know about.

1. Poor Food Quality in Delivery (14th January 2025):

I ordered Chicken Tikka for home delivery, and it was extremely poorly prepared — dry, tasteless, and almost inedible. It felt like it was made without any attention to basic cooking standards, let alone taste.

2. Terrible Dine-In Experience (18th May 2025 – Thane, Manpada branch):

I visited the restaurant with friends and we ordered Chicken Crispy as a starter.

The first serving was completely bland — only the outer coating had masala, and the chicken inside had no taste at all. Even the restaurant captain, Mr. Dilip, tasted it and agreed it wasn’t up to the mark.

He promised to replace it — and after waiting 45 minutes, the next serving arrived. The aroma was good, and the masala seemed fine, but shockingly, the chicken was undercooked. It was so raw and chewy that I genuinely couldn't swallow it.

I again called Mr. Dilip, clearly told him I did not want any complimentary items — I simply wanted a good meal, which sadly never came.

But the worst part was the billing experience:

They included the Chicken Crispy in the final bill, even though I clearly couldn’t eat it.

When I refused to pay for it, Mr. Dilip said they removed it — but instead, they removed the Chicken Manchow Soup (which I actually had and enjoyed), just because it was priced lower (₹220 vs ₹360).

After further argument, I had to go to the counter myself where the staff member removed the chicken crispy and added the soup back — something that should’ve taken 1 minute took 15 minutes of back-and-forth and unnecessary frustration.

Summary:

Food Quality: Highly inconsistent.

Service: Unprofessional and dismissive.

Billing Ethics: Manipulative and unclear.

The Only Positives:

Their Chicken Manchow Soup is excellent.

Murgh Musallam is also delicious — I had tried it on a past visit.

It is one of those restaurants in Borivali that continues to feel like home because of its food and hospitality.

This time, we began our meal with a bowl of Chicken Manchow Soup. It was served hot, and I enjoyed how it had a bold, flavorful taste without being overpowering. For starters, we ordered Veg Seekh Kebab, Mutton Seekh Kebab, and Chicken Pahadi Tikka. The Veg Seekh Kebab was nice, cooked well, and had the perfect earthy flavour. The Mutton Seekh Kebab was outstanding. It had a silky texture, was well-seasoned, and paired beautifully with the chutney. It was not chewy at all, and I really liked how smooth it felt with every bite. The Chicken Pahadi Tikka was equally good. The chicken was tender, juicy, and cooked with a light smokiness that made it enjoyable.

For the mains, I ordered Jeera Rice with Dal Tadka. The dal had a nice garlic tempering with the right amount of cumin, and together with the rice it felt wholesome and comforting. The Chicken Tikka Masala came with soft pieces of chicken in a thick gravy that had a good balance of spices. It went really well with the Tandoori Roti, which was crisp on the edges and soft in the middle. The Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was the last dish. It was mildly spiced, had a smoky taste from the wok, and the flavours were balanced in a way that made it enjoyable till the last bite.

As we were about to finish, we couldn’t resist ordering the Chicken Masala Lollipop, which has always been a family favorite. It was crispy, spicy, and coated beautifully with sauce. It was the highlight of the evening. The chicken inside was fresh and well-cooked, and every bite reminded me why I have loved this dish here for years.

The food at Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar is consistently good, and the staff make the experience even better. They are polite, attentive, and always welcoming. This restaurant is more of a family place, and the presence of a bar only adds to the variety without taking away from its warm atmosphere.

From the moment I walked in, I noticed that the place has a lively vibe. It isn’t fancy, but it’s clean, well-lit, with comfortable seating, and somehow retains a sense of casual warmth. The staff were welcoming and attentive, which made me feel at ease with the menu.

Because I couldn’t resist, I ordered the Tandoori Pomfret, Chicken Ghee Roast, and Butter Chicken Thali; also tried their mocktails. The Pomfret was fresh, cooked with good char on the edges, and well-marinated—its taste reminded me of classic Malvani flavours without being too overpowering. The Chicken Ghee Roast had that deliciously rich, buttery flavour and a nice mix of spices that made it a hit (my 7-year-old loved it). The Butter Chicken Thali served with rice and breads was solid—comforting, satisfying.

I also tried their Prawn Koliwada, which came out crisp and flavourful. The mocktails added fun to the meal; I had one fruity concoction and another with salty kick, both well balanced.

One thing to note: the menu is wide. Not only seafood, but also non-veg and veg options are there. But seafood is the highlight, and that’s what most people come for. Portions are generous, so you won’t leave hungry.

What could be better: since it’s a popular place, especially on weekends, there was some waiting for a table. Also, a couple of side breads (chapatis / bhakari) weren’t quite as good—they seemed a little underwhelming in texture. Ambience-wise, it gets noisy during peak hours; not the place for a super quiet meal, but excellent for a casual, enjoyable dinner.

All in all, Jai Hind Lunch Home in Thane is an excellent pick if you want good coastal and seafood fare, friendly service, and value for money. I’ll definitely be going back — maybe next time to try some of their other thalis and seafood specialties., name_person=Swapnil Tamhankar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=7 months ago, review=🌟6 star experience🌟

I would have given a higher rating if I could. This place stood out for its:
1. Food

3. ⁠Service/Staff
(well, what else do you rate the place for)

We ordered:
1. Prawns ghee roast

3. ⁠Meen Gassi (Surmai)
4. ⁠Neer dosa
5. ⁠Bhakari (rice)
6. ⁠Steam rice
7. ⁠Solkadhi

Surprisingly, all the items were 10/10 😀. Prawns ghee roast 🍤 was so mouth-watering 👄, I had it with neer dosa, bhakari and rice. Crab masala 🦀 was equally good, however I wished the crab was a little bigger in size. Surmai was made in a perfectly Mangalorean style. As someone who has stayed in Konkan for a few years, I can definitely vouch for their Solkadhi as well.

Ambience is very calm and soothing, with a touch of modern art. We went on a weekday for dinner and we didn’t get any waiting (probably because the place is new).

Server took his time to understand our requirement, answered all our questions patiently(yes I do ask a lot when it comes to fish 🐠) and got us exactly what we needed. Service time was moderate.

They serve specialities from Mangalore, Konkan, Goa, Kerala, Tamil Nadu. I can’t vouch for other cuisines, but Mangalorean dishes were prefection to the T.

My brother and I are always on a lookout for authentic restaurants serving fish in Thane (trust me we’ve tried many). Since we’re Mangaloreans, fish 🐟 is a part of our staple diet and hence we’re deeply critical of its quality. And I kid you not, I was blown away by the quality of the fish here and I would definitely recommend this place to all the fish lovers in Thane.

Must try - Prawns Ghee Roast 🍤

We opted for the Non-Veg buffet, and the spread was outstanding. Not only were the Punjabi and Mughlai dishes delicious, but the Chinese selections were equally remarkable.
Starters were the highlight for me — Amritsari Fish Fry, Fish Tikka, and Garlic Prawns were absolutely mouth-watering. Even the vegetarian starters exceeded expectations; Crispy Corn and Cajun Potatoes with Crispy Lotus Stem were flavorful and addictive.

The Chaat and Pizza counters were delightful as well — especially the Dahi Bhalla, Dahi Puri, and freshly prepared Pizza.

Moving to the Main Course, the Kashmiri Pulao, Hong Kong Noodles, and Crab Curry stood out and were cooked to perfection.

A few tips:
If you prefer a quieter dining experience, opt for lunch as the place is usually less crowded. Nights, weekends, and festival days tend to be packed.

A special mention to the staff and the chef — extremely polite, warm, and hospitable. We arrived late yet they waited for us patiently and ensured we had a great experience.

Donna Deli – Bandra West | Saturday Dinner Review

📍 Location & First Impressions
Donna Deli sits right on SV Road, Bandra, a short stroll from Khar Road Station so if you’re planning to drive, God be with you. If you're walking in, the white-washed European façade welcomes you like you’ve entered a Pinterest board.
Pro Tip: If it’s a weekend, reservation is non-negotiable. This place fills up quicker than your WhatsApp family group on Diwali morning.

🍽️ What We Tried

1. Truffle Pizza

Creamy, crispy, indulgent basically everything you want from a pizza that wears truffle like a crown. If royalty had a flavor, this would be it.

2. Truffle Fries

Yes, more truffle. Don’t judge.
We inhaled these while waiting for our drinks. Perfectly crisp, generously tossed, and honestly… finished too soon.

3. Donna’s Signature Drinks

We tried a bunch of their mocktails (let’s just say the menu has more Donnas than a Bollywood family tree). Refreshing, quirky, and worth experimenting with.

Do not go by the looks.
These noodles pack flavour, comfort, and a bit of drama. Easily the winner and something you’ll crave again.

🛎️ Service

Shockingly fast.
I mean the food arrived before our mocktails.
They take the “fast” in fast-casual seriously.

🌿 Ambience & Vibe

Donna Deli scores big here white décor, leafy corners, soft lighting, aesthetic touches everywhere. Instagram would approve. So would your date.

🚗 Parking & Access

Located right on SV Road

Walking distance from Khar station (recommended)

If coming by car, patience is a mandatory side dish

The ambiance truly sets the right tone.

However, the food didn’t match the expectations we had from the place.

What we tried:

Crispy Lamb Mandarin Style:
The flavours were nice and it did have a good crisp, but it turned out quite oily and a bit salty. Additionally, the lamb itself was hard to distinguish while chewing.

Crispy Prawn Cheung Fun:
This was the highlight of our meal. The prawns were extremely fresh, and the dish had a perfectly balanced taste. Definitely recommended.

Mandarin Fried Rice in Lotus Leaf (Chicken):
Expected this to be a standout, but it was fairly average and didn’t have the depth of flavour we anticipated.

Highly recommend, name_person=Noora Dmello}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=6 months ago, review=The space transitions beautifully and is definitely a highlight of the experience at Bombay Daak. The sun roof, the all glass facade, adds a wonderful charm to the cosy space. The open kitchen also made

10/10 would recommend if you’re feeling a bit bougie and want to impress your date. It’s tucked away enough for it to be a discovery, but also buzzing to not feel like you’re the only people to discover it- a balance that’s so rare.

We ordered quite a few things from the menu, but the highlight of it all were two things: the Pork & Smoke, which was the best thing I’ve tried in a while. Really smoky, succulent, meal-in-your-mouth bits of pork belly, over a mash, and layered with spices, herbs, a little bits of funk. So, so satisfying. If you eat pork, don’t miss it!

The other highlight was the Rasam inspired cocktail- blew our collective socks off. Such a refined cocktail, and so seasonable. Despite the impressive technique, it didn’t feel over intellectual and genuinely had a rasam after taste.

The rest was fine, nothing to write home about. But definitely worth frequent visits (if you can get a spot!), name_person=Sumit Sen}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Where do I even begin? The vibe, obviously. Imagine a dive bar, but it decided to clean up its act and look classy for once. That’s Bombay Daak. I’m a sucker for dive bars, and this one just gets it. Dark, moody, but still modern enough to make you go “okay, this is cool.” And the music, oh the music. In true Bangalore fashion, they dropped “Santhoshake,” that was it. I was emotionally invested.

Now the food, let me tell you, they had me at Shikaar Ka Achaar. Rabbit preserve in some mango-pickle-style masala, served with pav. I’m not exaggerating when I say I could eat that every day and still not get bored. The rest of the food was great too, but that rabbit? Unreal.

And then came Whistle Podu, a gin-based rasam cocktail. I know, sounds like chaos in a glass, but it worked. Refreshing, a little spicy, and very “what the hell, why is this so good?” kind of moment.

Service? Quick, friendly, and totally on point.

In short, go to Bombay Daak. Eat, drink, vibe. Thank me later (preferably with a Whistle Podu in hand)., name_person=Maanush Dev}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The food, the staff, the drinks everything is just an experience.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=If you love cocktails that celebrate Indian flavours, this is the place to be.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Very small space Seating a bit too close to each other.}"]

Chili’s has always been known for its dependable food quality, and that part still remains intact. We ordered the Chicken Platter, which comes with a nice customisation option. The portion size was good, the flavours were balanced, and everything was served hot and well-prepared. It’s the kind of comfort food Chili’s is known for, and it didn’t disappoint.

For drinks, I tried their Mango Mocktail, and it was easily one of the highlights of the evening. Refreshing, smooth, and perfectly sweet — I liked it so much that I ended up ordering it twice. Their beer selection was also good, maintaining the familiar Chili’s standard.

However, a few things held the experience back from being a full 5-star visit. The first noticeable issue was the pre-added 10% tip on the bill. While I fully support tipping for good service, adding it automatically and at a relatively high percentage didn’t feel right — especially considering the level of service we received. The service wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t exceptional enough to justify a mandatory 10% charge. Tips should always feel voluntary and earned, not forced.

The ambience also felt different compared to the older Chili’s outlets. One thing that always made Chili’s special was its distinct American pub-style vibe — warm lighting, rustic interiors, and a lively but cozy atmosphere. The Powai outlet, unfortunately, doesn’t quite capture that same charm. The décor and layout feel more like a typical modern Indian pub, lacking the signature Chili’s personality that many of us associate with the brand. It’s decent, but it doesn’t stand out the way earlier Chili’s interiors used to.

That said, the environment is still comfortable for dining, and the place is clean, spacious, and well-maintained. The overall quality of food and drinks remains trustworthy, and if you’re looking for a casual evening out with good food, Chili’s Powai is still a reliable choice.

The place has a very relaxed yet elegant vibe. As soon as you walk in, you notice the clean, modern interiors with a warm touch — not too fancy, not too casual — just the right atmosphere to enjoy a good Italian meal. The service was polite and attentive without being overbearing, which made the whole experience even better.

We ordered two dishes: the Arrabiatta Pasta and the Vegetariana Pizza.

The Arrabiatta Pasta was absolutely spot on. It had the perfect balance of flavors — the tomato sauce was rich and vibrant, with just the right amount of spice that hits you pleasantly at the back of your throat without overwhelming the dish. The pasta was cooked al dente, which gave it that slight bite that’s so essential but often missed. Every forkful felt hearty and comforting, exactly how a good pasta should.

The Vegetariana Pizza was equally impressive. Made in a true Neapolitan style with a thin, airy, and slightly charred crust, it came loaded with colorful fresh vegetables — bell peppers, zucchini, mushrooms, and more. The mozzarella was creamy, and the vegetables were cooked just right, still holding a bit of crunch and freshness. What stood out the most was how light the pizza felt — unlike the heavy, greasy ones you often find — yet it was packed with flavor in every bite.

Both dishes were served piping hot, and the portions were generous without going overboard. It really felt like the kitchen team cared about every plate they sent out.

Overall, Gustoso completely delivered on what we were hoping for. If you’re craving truly authentic Italian food, especially pizza or pasta done the traditional way, this place should be very high on your list. Younion season 2 is something you shouldn't miss out on.

Location: Younion is located at one of the most happening places of the town known for some really good places to hangout and night life i.e. Kamla Mills, Lower Parel.

About the Place:
A perfect place for a perfect night out along with your friends is what we would say. Younion has everything that will impress you. Each wall is beautifully decorated.   The artificial plants hanging through ceiling, nicely spaced seating arrangements, amazing music played over here and the crowd that visits this place helps to create that perfect vibe.

Younion has more than 300 shots and 25 variety of new cocktails at an affordable rates on their menu for your gang. They also have 50 new LIIT's & the menu is also made vast with more 80 dishes, largest pizza, burger & Dimsums. The food over here is also good. They have some really good fusion food perfect to have along with your drinks.

Shittake mushroom, with truffle mayo & cheese. It was one of the best burger we have had in recent times. Highly Recommended..!!

Avocado green out pizza

Many friends told me to try their garlic‑butter specials, so we ordered garlic‑butter prawns for my 5‑year‑old, and she devoured them. The garlic‑butter sauce left on her plate was so good, I happily took it with my rice.

My 7‑year‑old, not a seafood fan, enjoyed her beloved reshmi kebab again—soft, flavorful, and exactly to her taste.

We ordered tandoori pomfret for my husband and me. We got to choose our fish and it was cooked to perfection. Spicy smoky and delicious we loved every bite and did not leave a crumb behind

My husband had ordered fish and chips thinking the kids might not eat the reshmi kebab but they did not touch the fish and chips at all

Not wanting to waste food we packed the untouched fish and chips the remaining prawn curry and rice. Later that night we gave it to an elderly lady living in a tent near our hotel and she was very grateful

However, my experience was far from what was portrayed.

Upon arrival, I was informed that the family section was on the second floor, requiring us to climb steep steps. The first floor housed the bar area, where a group of visibly drunk individuals were loudly using foul language. To reach the family section, one has to pass through this bar, which, in appearance and ambiance, felt more like a local dive bar.

When we reached the second floor, the so-called family section, I was immediately disappointed. The space was extremely dark and had a shady atmosphere. Apart from us, only one other couple arrived, but they chose to leave almost instantly. I also wanted to leave, but out of courtesy, I decided to stay and dine since we had already entered.

The setting was uninviting—dimly lit, poorly maintained, and eerily empty on Valentine's Day, a time when most restaurants are bustling. The place was dirty, the menu card was covered in dust, and the food was far below average. Additionally, the seating was uncomfortably low compared to the height of the table, making dining awkward.

Finally managed to get one thing of my bucket list of restaurants which I always wanted to visit. Located at Level 00 like most of the other restaurants at Sahara Star, Namak serves authentic Indian cuisine. Chic ambience, live kitchen, soothing music, lipsmacking food, prompt and courteous service; this sums up our experience at Namak. We preferred the Chef's recommended menu here since it is a three course meal, along with starters, main course and dessert.\\n\\nWe were welcomed with an inaugural drink - a refreshing mix of pineapple juice and mint leaves. Moving to the appetizers, it was a platter of 3 starters - Tandoori Malai Paneer Roll, Chenna Palak Ki Shami and Shimbi Paneer Ki Seekh. All three contain paneer but of all my absolute favourite is Chenna Palak Ki Shami. This Palak with cheese filling kebab literary melts in your mouth, the chef has done a fabulous job by preparing a veg version of this all time favourite kebab. Tandoori Malai Paneer Roll was also brilliant, again Paneer extremely soft and fresh marinated in pickling spices if onion and mint malai cheese grilled in tandoor to perfection. Now moving to the mains there were three vegetables Khade Masale Ke Paneer, Tripoliya Subzi and Sua Dakhni Saag which is Namak's version of Sarson Da Saag. Of the three I would say Tripoliya Subzi - mix veggies was the best, one of the best I have had in a long time. Signature dish at Namak and a must have at Namak. Sua Dakhni - spinach based veggie gives this amazing smokey taste, which I personally love. This is due to roasted garlic. Again a must try for those who like Sarson Da Saag.\\n\\nAll these veggies were accompanied with the Thikri Dal Makhani, creamy and super yummy! For breads we called for Zaffrani Paratha which is a layered paratha along with tonnes of Saffron in it. Loved this paratha as well, another must try! Post this we ended the mains with Tarkari Biryani served with Raita. Biryani was superb had layers of rice with veggies and spices. Finally moving to dessert we had the signature one Shaad-e-Jamun which is mini jamuna baked and layered with rabdi. A must try dessert, don't miss this for anything.\\n\\nOne of the most memorable experience, one of the most memorable evening, all thanks to Namak Sahara Star. Special thank you to the chef Karan Singh who prepared this delicious meal for us. Also our server Saeed, for being extremely courteous and helpful. A must visit,  especially when celebrating any special occasions with your friends or family. Hope to come back here sooner than later!\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"Great service very tasty food and a soothing ambiance ..... must visit place\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"The biryani had a lovely flavour of spices and the chicken too was cooked well.\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"person_name\":null,\"time_line\":null,\"review\":\"Nice ambience, polite staff and good quality food being served\",\"guided_block\":{}}"]

🍰 Desserts: A Sweet Finish
Japanese Cheesecake – Light, fluffy, and delicately sweet. It was a delightful way to end the meal. The presentation was also spot-on.
Molten Chocolate Cake – Rich, gooey, and absolutely indulgent. The chocolate oozed out perfectly, and it was a hit among all of us.
⭐ Service & Overall Experience
The service at Kofuku was exceptional. The staff was attentive, knowledgeable, and helped guide us through the menu with genuine warmth. Everything — from the food and drinks to the ambiance and hospitality — was top-notch.

Highly Recommend., name_person=Mangesh Jadhav _ MJ}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a year ago, review=So, on August 24th, I found myself at this spot—not because I wanted to, but because there was literally nowhere else around, and my stomach was staging a protest. From the outside, the place looked like it might be hiding gold in its walls, so I thought, "Why not?" But as soon as I stepped inside, I noticed something odd: there were more waiters than customers. It felt like I’d walked into a waiter convention, with me as the only guest.

Now, onto the food—or whatever it was. I started with the masala papad. To my surprise, the only "masala" on it was an overwhelming abundance of tomatoes and onions. I considered adding some spice myself, but the salt and pepper shakers were clearly on strike. Not a grain of salt or pepper was willing to escape their cozy little homes.

Next up was the chicken manchow soup. For a whopping ₹320, I expected something decent. Instead, I got a bland, lukewarm concoction that made me question my life choices. Then came the butter chicken, which, as everyone knows, should be sweet and creamy. But no, this butter chicken had other plans. The chicken pieces were rubbery enough to bounce off the walls, and the sauce was missing any trace of sweetness. The tandoori roti? Let’s just say I wasn’t sure if I was supposed to eat it or repurpose it as a frying pan.

In conclusion, for the price, this place is a hard pass. reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Having lived and worked in Japan, albeit many moons ago, I was not expecting to be reminded of the tastes and feel of a typical izakaya in the land of the rising sun, in, of all places, Bandra, Mumbai.
We were ushered to our seating by a raucous welcome from the Kuuraku staff, which was more reminiscent of the Wankhede Stadium than a Japanese restaurant. But there was a effervescence about the staff at Kuuraku, reflecting the confidence that they have in their excellent food.
We ordered the Special Kushi Course, comprising 5 sticks of yakitori. The standout of this was the chicken tail. It was so good that we ordered two extra sticks of this, named bonjiri shio. We also ordered a portion of pork belly yakitori although this was very slightly disappointing as it was a little on the tough side. Another slight disappointment was the chargrilled asparagus wrapped in pork belly. Again, the pork belly wasn't as tender as I expected and the asparagus was a little small and fibrous. However, the edamame challenge was a lot of fun. The idea is to grab as much edamame as possible with one hand - and what you grab is what you get to eat. I used my goalkeeper hands to grab, what the server told me was an over par amount. The edamame was quite good too. The crunchy ebi roll was very generous too coming as a generous portion. The temperature of the rice was spot on as was the consistency. Could the quality of the rice be higher as in Japan? Well yes if you can get that rice but otherwise it really was excellent. The same goes for the pork rice. Here the consistency or the stickiness of the rice was more important than in the ebi roll and if they could get better rice it was be amazing. The slight disappointment was the inclusion of bell peppers. Heresy! Finally, the tea was served in a beautiful black pot, again, very true to Japan.
All in all this was an excellent place with a really true feel of Japan, helped also by the constant stream of Japanese music and the service was particularly excellent. A dinner on a fine day at this premium property was not destined to go well. Romano's, a restaurant which I had visited twice before, known for its close to flawless service & dishes, typical Italian style preparation and cuisine, and not to forget the sea bass, which was the best ever I had eaten anywhere in the same level hotels, but now it was all history. Today, the same restaurant had a below-average experience in stock for me.

Dishes took longer than the expected time. I had ordered a salmon and a sea bass and was told that it would take 20 and 25 mins respectively, but it took quite longer than that. While the salmon had a flaw, which upon complaining was first met with a response that it was good according to them, but they eventually agreed to replace it. Needless to say, taste buds do differ. Even on the second count, it didn't taste as it normally does. Surely not the first time I have tried it, and in fact, I have tried it in the same property a few times, and it was delicious previously, but this time, no offence intended, tasted weird. The second dish sea bass was not as good as last time, but still good enough. Again, the portion was quite small. The preparation was also different compared to last time.

The bread basket which is otherwise served, wasn't in this case ( I saw other customers getting one ). Again, this could be because I was availing a food festival offer. Even the mocktails took over 15 mins to be served, which is surprising, and instructions of less ice weren't followed. The blue mocktail was on a mild sweet and tangy side, and tasted good. The yellow one was average. The quantity of mocktails was medium. The restaurant was not too crowded either, so the wait time is indeed surprising.

Contrary to the case in the same level hotels, no one came to check in how the dishes were, and it was not easy to call the servers. The servers took a long time to come, and even when complained to someone in the coat ( I assume, a supervisor ), I was told sorry, but nothing changed. The supervisor didn't look much concerned about the experience and never came back to check if the concerns were resolved or not.

Attempts to resolve the concern at a senior level later ( since they weren't resolved in the restaurant properly ) went in vain. I was told that the issue would be looked into. However, my further messages were met with no response, which talks loudly about how much the senior level cares for the customers.

I wouldn't feel like going here again given their overall remiss approach. This wasn't even a four-star service. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min}, time_line=3 months ago, review=We were looking for a corporate dinner party venue and that’s when we thought of trying this restaurant, since a few of our colleagues had already visited and had loved the food. The restaurant is located in a prominent Bandra West location, which makes it very easy to find. Once inside, you’ll notice that the space is spread across different floors – one with a DJ, another with karaoke, and the top floor dedicated to dining with some pleasant background music. It immediately gives you the sense that this is not just a place to eat but a full experience.

The ambiance here is truly something unique. The lighting, especially, stands out as it has all been designed using musical instruments like drums and other elements, which gives the interiors a creative and rare vibe. It’s not something you get to see often in restaurants, and it definitely adds to the overall charm of dining here. It sets the perfect mood for a fun evening out, whether in a group or with family.

Coming to the food, we started with the Vada Takoyaki, which at first glance may look like a simple potato vada but is actually a brilliant fusion. Served piping hot in six pieces with a delicious white sauce, crunchy dry chutneys, and flavorful toppings, this dish really impressed us with its creativity and taste. Next, we tried the Gochujang Paneer, another must-try. The paneer was crispy fried, topped with fried garlic, and had a creamy yoghurt base inside. The balance of crunch and flavor was outstanding, making it one of the best fusion dishes we’ve had in a long time. To complement the food, I ordered a cucumber and mint mocktail with lime soda, served chilled without sugar. It was incredibly refreshing and paired perfectly with the rich flavors of the food. Finally, we rounded off with the Farmhouse Pizza, served on flatbread with generous toppings of onions, black olives, and mushrooms layered under gooey, melting cheese. Every bite was wholesome, satisfying, and top notch in taste.

Despite it being a busy weekend, the service was prompt and the staff made sure every guest was well taken care of. Their attentiveness and welcoming nature added a lot to the overall dining experience. All in all, this restaurant has everything going for it – delicious and unique food, a vibrant ambiance, and friendly staff. If you are in Bandra, this place is definitely worth a visit and stands out as a must-try., name_person=Ronit Gaikwad}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Very few spots in Mumbai with Rock music or Karaoke downstairs if that’s your vibe. - Amazing location, the area was more than big enough for us. The have one small space and one large space divided, as per your need & party size you can choose one or both.
- Decor was on point. They have their own vendor for the same who has monopoly, but Shweta knows her stuff, and will help you achieve the best possible decor in your budget. Totally Trustworthy, just be clear and detailed in your brief and references
- Food - Bang on. Worth every penny, all of our guests mentioned great stuff & compliments about the food, starters and welcome drinks. On request, the starters where circulated for much longer than the usual time as well. The staff service was very well executed too. Kudos to Subhash sir.

CONS -
- The DJ and lights vendor (Sanjay), who they have appointed, and who has monopoly there, was the only thing that didn't work out for us. Which we agreed on, also extra amounts where paid for stage lightings as well for Dance performances, as they weren't a part of the DJ or Decor Setup.

- The DJ was not informed that its a double shift, hence he didn't start the soft music sessions on time. We know this because he actually said to us "Your sangeet and function starts at 6, why do you need music from 4 PM"?. The double shift was booked from 4 PM - 10 PM.
- The vendor (Sanjay)  was very pro active with us, till the payment went to him. Post that, everything was a blunder.

So overall, i would say this place is lovely, in terms of the food, venue and decor. Located in Vile Parle East, this restaurant and bar serves some amazingly fresh and quality dishes. The primary cuisine served is North Indian and Chinese. They also have Mangalorean dishes on the menu which are a must try. They have a nice bar with a wide variety of drinks to choose from.
The ambience is nice with dim lights and a wall full of quotes. The seating is comfortable. The overall look and feel is like a family restaurant and bar. The service was prompt to start with Mahesh taking down the orders. However they took a reasonable amount of time to get all the dishes.

The mocktails we had were Cinderella and Berry Blast. Both these were juice based drinks. Berry blast has Cranberry and Apple juice with a touch of honey.
Cindrella has orange juice and fresh lime which makes it very refreshing.

The food we had was all very good in terms of quality and quantity. I would rate it a value for money place.

We had Murg Toorki which was Chicken Tikka marinated with Cheese and this was delicious. The chicken was cooked to perfection, juicy and charred perfectly. This tasted even better with the mint coriander chutney.

Coriander Chicken Dry was a Chinese appetizer, this was again very good. Herbaceous flavour with garlic and spring onions. Again well cooked Chicken. Very satisfying.

For the main course we had Chicken Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa. My favourite and everything was perfect. Must have when here. Highly recommended.

The Cheese Garlic Naan here is not the usual Naan with the Garlic and Cheese outside. Here it's stuffed inside and is very wholesome.
We had Chicken Betabi which is a red gravy similar to Butter Chicken in many ways with shredded chicken in a luscious velvety gravy.

For dessert we had a sizzling walnut brownie with ice cream. This was fresh and well made.

This place even has outdoor seating which is accessible only post rains. I am totally in awe of the simplicity and the no nonsense kind of approach to serving good quality food.

I am totally coming back here again with my gang for a great meal.

Till next time Bon Appetit!, name_person=Varun Poduval}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good Ambience, Good Service, quality and tasty Food ,}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=They serve Chinese, BBQ,North Indian, seafood, biriyani, deserts and beverages.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Tasted really well with the mild flavours of the butter garlic chicken.}"]

["{guided_block={}, time_line=8 years ago, review=Hope you guys remember U-Turn . This is the same place been segmented to Round About. Located on the 4th floor segmented to indoor and outdoor. Well I opted for outdoor as the climate was quite pleasant(Oh Yes..!! The outdoor is covered (With a temporary rooftop for the rains) Outdoor has and additional 3 shamiyana seating which can be occupied as per your convenience .

Keys Points

Good Place for Sheesha: Sheesha Lovers this is yet another joint for sheesha’s. They have a good variety of Hookahs .
Indoor Seating: Hookah indoor….!! Yeah you heard it right. It ain’t Smokey inside .Management said they are equipped with good ventilation and air condition so one won’t face any issue

Cocktails & Moctails

Shall describe a line on each
a. BLUE LAGOON- Vodka + Blue curacao + Sprite + Ice
b. RED WINE WITH SANGRIA – Was refreshing. Name is self descriptive
c. FRUIT PUNCH – Real Juices blend together with Crushed Ice (Pineapple, orange, mango , pineapple)
d. GIMLET- Gin + Fresh Lime
e. LONG ISLAND ICE TEA- It was the good nothing exceptional
f. RED BOMB- Couldn’t identify the flavor but tasted ok.
g. 3G- Guava + Rock Salt
h. Pineapple Mojito- had good punch of mint

All the cocktails tasted well. But was more happy with the moctails.

======================================================================

Starters

1.Vegetarian

JALAPENO POPPERS
They were the best. Jalapeno hit was just perfect with cheese guoeng from inside. Break it into half an enjoy served along with a dip and salad but would suggest you have it without the dip.. Would recommend this for sure.

ALOO MUTTER TIKKA
The tikka was amazing in terms of texture, flavors and presentation. Expected the peas to be mashed and mixed with the potatoes but the mixture contained the whole peas which turned out good.

PANEER WANTONS
King sized wantons with Paneer chili stuffed in it. Had good balance in terms of taste. Wantons were crispy. This was surprisingly really good.

CHILI CHEESE TOAST
Since we had a shudh shahakri member. This was ordered. But we feasted on this .cheese with a good blend of onion, bell pepper, chilly , tomatoes. I feel the entire portion was empty within seconds. Lip Smacking.Highly recommended.

--------------------------

Non Vegetarian

FISH FINGERS
These are exactly finger shaped, Thin and long. Fish used here is only rawas. Quite fresh and crispy coat with tartar Dip. It’s very tempting and shall opt you to have the next one.

KALMI KABAB
Man these guys have nailed it. No flaw in anything. Texture, flavors and all were simply mind blowing. How do you guys get such a big chop. 3 pieces are just enough for the entire evening. The kababs were properly tandoored.

CHICKEN FLAMINGO
Presentation was simple but so nicely done. Stuffed chicken breast cut into 5 or more pieces served with salad. Stuffing had components like mushrooms, spices, onions, spinach. Portions are a bit massive so please check before you order for it.

PRAWNS KADIPATHA
Kadipatha was the star flavor (which is curry leaves), so here prawns are tossed with curry leaves , oil and mustard seeds. Prawn with tail was very fresh and Juicy. You can the curry leaf Flavors right in the first bite and the mustard seed gives the kick. Fabulous..!!!

FISH STICKS
This was another surprise, rawas fish with olive shot. This was perfect and quite different. Tasted really good.

======================================================================

Mains

BUTTER CHICKEN
This was perfect butter chicken with tandoored chicken shred pieces . Best partnered with jeera rice.

Deserts

Sizzling Brownie

Apparently, it was. Instead of simply pouring the measured wine back, the bartender (Bhavesh) decided to keep the extra wine for himself and snapped, “You wanted the standard serving - this is it.”

Obviously near airport, you will face typical traffic situation to reach the hotel but once inside you are transported to completely different world.
Drive way of hotel is a certainly a steep slope you will not find anywhere in Mumbai drive 😉
Usher and Valet service was quick and huge lobby of hotel was magnificent with light colour lights and decor.
The Merchants is just one floor above the lobby level, you can walk on the stairs enjoying arry of chandeliers and Mumbai inspired wall murals.
Grand Entrance of restaurant makes it welcoming and helpful staff guides you to comfortable soft seats. Huge space divided into various sections with open partitions overlooking respective kitchen area with traditional shape pot ovens make it interesting to watch chefs art.
Mr. Shambhunath was courteous and helpful to guide us for selecting options from wide verity of menu.
1. Pasta with selection of Cheese Fondue sauce was perfect preparation and presentation. Temptation of trying a bite without waiting for next dish explain its star rating.
2. Kids selection of Pizza with Chicken Tikka and green chilli addition was big in size but was finished in no time.
3. Veg kebab platter arrived with controlled roasted paneer, broccoli with mustard oil seasoning and hot succulent kebab, which took some time to explore mostly due to appreciation for earlier two dishes.
Complementary chicken salt pepper and paneer tikka was very tasty and well made. Thanks for the offer.
Literally icing on the cake was offer for dessert on the house by Mr. Shambhunath which led us to trying small bites of verity of dessert items.

They were almost closing, but still accommodated us, which I really appreciated.

The vibe is outstanding — luxurious yet calming and homely at the same time. Lots of plants, beautiful artwork, and plenty of seating. Loved the ambience from the moment I walked in.

Starters

We ordered Lamb Chops, Ceylon Black Pork, and Chicken Tokku Masala.
•	Ceylon Black Pork completely stole the show — soft, flavourful, and absolutely delicious.
•	Chicken Tokku Masala came second.
•	Surprisingly, my usual favourite Lamb Chops ranked third this time, though still good.

The Sampler Experience

While deciding on curries, we were unsure what to order. The staff brought us a sampler of different curries and rices, and the waiter explained each item patiently. This was genuinely an amazing experience and helped us choose perfectly.

Mains

We went with:
•	Prawn Yellow Coconut Curry
•	Mutton Kolumbu Curry

Both were good, but the Prawn Yellow Coconut Curry was OUT OF THIS WORLD — easily the best dish of the entire meal. It was finger-licking good.
It tasted amazing with both Malabar Parotta and Appam, but we loved it so much that we ordered plain rice — and that combination was heaven on a plate.

The Mutton Kolumbu paired really well with parotta.

Next, we ordered the Boneless Mutton Biryani. This was a pulao-style biryani (not dum), and I actually loved it. Soft mutton, beautifully spiced rice, and super flavourful.

To finish, we ordered Rasam, served hot with papad. It was the perfect conclusion to an already amazing meal.

Overall

Yes, the place is slightly on the higher side price-wise, but the taste, service, and overall experience are absolutely worth it.

But unfortunately, that’s where the positives ended for me.

It is very rare to find a Christian Moreau Chablis in India, and it was nice to see this wine on the menu at Le Cirque, Mumbai, and I ordered the same for my dinner.

Christian Moreau is one of the oldest and most respected domains in Chablis.
Wine has fruit notes like apple, green apple, pear etc.
A very beautiful and amazing Chablis wine.

A great wine needs great food.
That’s where the restaurant failed badly, and food was below average.

Next a prawn based dish which was completely bad as well.

The Chef Kamlesh suggested a portion of Crème Brûlée + Tiramisu.

To conclude, the overall experience was far below expectations.

If you’re planning a special evening at Liv Eatery & Bar, a rooftop restaurant located in Wagle Estate, Thane, you might want to reconsider. Our recent visit turned out to be the worst dining experience we’ve had in a long time, leaving us frustrated, disappointed, and still hungry.

Location & Ambience: 2/5

Let’s start with the location – while the building itself is new and modern, the area around it is dusty, unhygienic, and gives off a creepy vibe, especially after sunset. Upon arrival, guests are required to check in at the reception to get an entry pass before heading up to the 14th floor via a lift.

As we stepped out onto the rooftop, the Valentine’s Day decoration with red heart-shaped props and crimson focus lights was meant to create a romantic atmosphere. Unfortunately, it felt cheap and borderline eerie, more like a setup from a low-budget horror flick than a cozy date spot.

Seating arrangements were a major letdown.
The tables for couples were tiny, cramped, and paired with uncomfortable chairs. Even the waitstaff admitted that the seating was impractical. They added an extra small table to accommodate our order, but it hardly helped. We spent the evening struggling for space rather than enjoying our time.

Our second dish was supposed to be a safe bet – Chicken Crispy, a personal favorite of my wife. What arrived was an utter disaster. The chicken was so rubbery and chewy that it felt like chewing gum. Adding to our misery, the restaurant is a smoker’s paradise. Smoke from nearby tables and bar counters constantly filled the air, making it unpleasant and suffocating for non-smokers like us.

Final Straw: We Left Hungry

Frustrated and dissatisfied, we left the place with half-empty stomachs and headed to another restaurant to salvage what was left of our evening. Thankfully, we finally had good food elsewhere, but the damage to our mood was already done.

Liv Eatery & Bar is heavily overrated, and the reality falls far short of the hype. If you value good food, attentive service, and a pleasant atmosphere, this is not the place for you.

My fourth visit to this French / Mediterranean restaurant was filled with fantastic delights, crafted dishes, amazing interactions, and sweet surprises throughout the dinner.

We were warmly welcomed at the restaurant by head chef, Mr Minocha, who named a few specialities and why they deserved consideration, and wow! -- all of them were outstanding; more on that, later. In a few minutes of our arrival, we were served complimentary kiwi mocktails, which had a high-powered soda and were mildly sweet; it didn't take long for the team to catch our taste buds for mocktails. We ordered a blueberry-based mocktail and a mango lassi, and both were authentic. The former was reasonably sweet with a significant amount of fruit % made with medium-power soda, whilst the latter had a rich % of alphonso mango [ and not concentrate ] content, unlike other same-level places where mango lassi is likely to have more of concentrate and yoghurt %.

Till the time the main course was getting ready, we were served a small plate -- Avvolto Avocado -- which was a small, soft roll containing mashed avocado with a dash of jalapeno flavour. In Pizzas, we were recommended Truffle tartufo, and gosh! The smell has started doing the talking and managed to dominate our sensations. The arugula was a skosh scratchy on the tongue, but that could easily be kept aside without affecting the taste of the pizza; it could not supersede the rich parmesan spread on the crispy layers. Next came the soups, and the chef had to do some convincing; I ain't someone who has much liking for soups. But the chef had won here; his nice smile had words written all over it. If the aroma wouldn't be all over one, then just a sip would send one in an Elysian mood. The porcini cream soup with its truffle foam, which looked like a cappuccino, was creamy and so delicious that I could keep having it.

And now came the main course -- Pan-seared Chilean Sea Bass and Lobster. The former was arguably the best I have had hitherto; A medium-sized portion served with sauteed veggies and mashed potatoes alongside, it was perfectly cooked and easy to slice that I couldn't help but scoff it quickly. If one weren't to mince for words, no words would really describe the taste; one would have to nosh it to feel it. Meanwhile, we ordered a cranberry-based mocktail, and as per our instructions, it was mildly sweet with medium-power soda; this was notable given that mocktails which are significantly or entirely cranberry-based cannot be kept away from high sweetness. And this was just another example of scrupulousness from the restaurant.

In the desserts, we were treated to a De-constructed Tiramisu, a famous Italian dish. Having a different presentation and girded by lady fingers and creme and chocolate cuts on top, it had a rich coffee texture and was brownish and spongier than the ones I have had in same-level restaurants. The size was small. The Classical-flavoured Cannoli with three flavours was a roll filled with flavoured, reasonably sweet creme, albeit one of the flavours was insipid, and possibly a change of flavours would find more takers. The chef agreed to my request to replace the original ice cream, and the chocolate ice cream [ sans almonds ] was delicious and made up for the cannolis. The size was large overall. Another off-the-menu dessert, whose name I have forgotten, which was offered to us, too, was a chocolate-based dessert whose layer was artistically molten by liquid chocolate to form a crater. It was delightful too.

Throughout our dinner, Mr Lopes and his teammates were around to ensure that our requirements were looked after, and satisfyingly so, and we were given notable suggestions from time to time; we enjoyed our chat with everyone, in particular, Mr Lopes. It was also nice to catch up with Mr Minocha earlier. I would also like to thank Mr Srinivas for personally looking into the reservation. CLAY offers an impressive and highly photogenic setting. The poolside seating is particularly appealing and creates a relaxed, resort-like atmosphere. ⸻

Service

⸻

Food & Beverages

We ordered a combination of pasta (two varieties), veg starters, several non-veg dishes, and mocktails.

Pricing

Overall Experience

CLAY is an excellent choice for ambience, relaxation, and photography. The service and mocktails stand out positively. However, to deliver a complete value-for-money experience, the food quality requires enhancement.

Recommendation

"The House you want to be at"

I have been through this lane quite a few times but never actually noticed this place until today. The restaurants on this lane have a small entrance so they are hard to notice if you are passing by but they are grand like this one. From the outside it appears that it can accommodate only a handful of people but when you step in you can see the actual picture. They have a lower outdoor seating, a lower indoor seating, an upper outdoor seating and an upper indoor seating.

The coziest and the most house-like feeling is the upper indoor seating - It is made like "The House" and has different types of tables. The lower outdoor seating is the most happening with a few high tables and nice cheerful music. Mosquitos can be a concern in the winter evenings but coils can be arranged. Our wait staff Nitesh was knowledgeable and Bartender - Anwar shaikh was good at his skills too.

Drinks/Beverages

We sat in the happening area by which I mean in the lower outdoor seating which made us order a cocktail and some mocktails. The cocktail was the kind of I like - With Bourbon Whisky. It is named as BOURBON HOUSE - it is a mixture of Jim Beam, Bacardi and Vodka. The beer glass with Jim Beam sticker looked amazing and the cocktail was even better. It was garnished with a slice of Orange and some leaves over it.

One of the mocktails we loved was THE HOUSE DELIGHT - According to them, they have it in different variety like Kiwi, Watermelon and some other options; we chose the KIWI based because Nitesh informed that it is the best of all and it actually turned out to be the best. It is a clear mocktail with in house mix with Kiwi as base with added soda, served in a Balloon glass. It had a proper not so sweet Kiwi taste. It is refreshing.

Food

Starters

To complement our cocktail, we ordered a dish to much upon. The all-time favorite and almost and the safest option - CHILLI CHEESE TOAST. It is just as expected and I am glad we ordered it. These were triangle bread toasted and topped with cheese, green chilli, onion and coriander (we requested to exclude tomato). It was crispy, spicy and cheesy at the same time and could be considered a perfect bar nibble.

The next dish is a perfect continental starter - GRILLED PANEER. We ordered this because The House is known for continental dishes. This is a perfect continental dish with Grilled paneer, mashed potato, Sauteed vegetables and Teriyaki sauce. I loved everything in here except the mashed potato as I am not a fan of potatoes. The dish is presented well, Paneer is soft and marinated well and the vegetables are boiled to perfection.
Mains

The House has a different concept in terms of main course. They don't have main course listed in the menu but they have daily specials which they write on a black board along with price. Out of the ones listed today, we went with the NAPOLEON PASTA - This is more of a white sauce penne pasta with a cheesy white sauce, exotic veggies and my favorite pasta bread. I so crave for these breads. Most of the times I agree to order pasta is because of these breads.

The pasta was Insta-worthy and hence available on my Instagram page too. The breads were a little soft and different from other breads that I have had, but we liked it too. Other items ordered were Pinacolada, The fruit punch & Venkatesh chicken. The house is listed under Rooftops collection. It has a smoking area and Wi-Fi too.

Despite being located at a busy intersection, the instant you come inside, you are taken to a tranquil and unexpectedly quiet environment. Amidst the dim lights and décor paying ode to the Goan theme, what we appreciated the most was the ample open space to move around and even dance (which our daughter did multiple times throughout the night).

FOOD:
Vegetable Cheese Rissois: Though the classic Portuguese fried pastry is usually filled with meat, we tried the vegetarian version and were not disappointed. It starts with a crumbly-soft bite which leads to a minced vegetables mixed with cheese that definitely melts in your mouth.

Mapusa Market toast with Cheese & Green Chilli: Coconut boys take on the chilli cheese toast with a twist. On first look it’s just your average cheese chilli toast, but one bite into it and you hit a tangy punch which took us by surprise…. It was mango aachaar! ‘Who would’ave thunk?’ This dish did have some mixed opinions!

Choris Chilli Fry: Choriz tossed with chilli, onion, tomato teamed up with warm, fluffy poee… we absolutely left licking our fingers. Would have gone for round two but there was more to be relished on the menu.

Grilled Squid Stuffed with Crab: A host suggestion that we absolutely jumped at the mention of! Crab meat tossed in Recheado, stuffed into a squid & grilled… a lot of effort goes into this. Hints of spice married with the sweetness of the crab meat and the bite of squid… a messy meal you must try at least once! Definitely big brownie points for the squid NOT being chewy.

Mushroom & vegetables slow cooked with Xacuti masala: A medley of steamed veggies (Mushroom, carrot, potato, cauliflower) tossed in a Xacuti gravy. You have an option of Poee or steamed rice to accompany it and we went with the latter. We requested them to hold back the spice a bit for our toddler & it’s wholesome, earthy, slightly-sweet coconut-ty broth was welcomed with a smack of the lips.

Serradura: This simple pudding can go awry in so many ways… And believe me, we've tasted some absolute disasters. But coconut boy absolutely nailed-it! The crumbly, biscuit dust alternated with fluffy, light whipped cream was what we devoured at the end of a great meal. Not too sweet, not too dense… just perfect.

Service: The service undoubtedly elevated our entire experience! We had Siddhesh giving us amazing recommendations and making sure we had everything we needed. Akbar stopped by with some fantastic banter, and last but not least, Faustin, whom our daughter adored and sat with virtually the entire dinner, allowing us to savour every bite!

SUMMING UP: If you love Goan food, it’s definitely an experience you do not want to miss. Right from the décor to the service, it’s comfy, cozy and warm.
