8/12 is my parents anniversary and exactly a year ago we arrived at Nara only to be turned away due to a staff party. One more attempt in between and it was fully booked.

This time i had booked the table only to be sure to have a table. There is outdoor seating too.

The hostess quick in finding our reservation and within seconds we were ushered into the restaurant and offered to choose our table which was a big plus as some places designate tables. The ambience was welcoming and elegant.

Our server Leishi arrived at our table with greetings and a smile to ask if we were comfortable. Within minutes, we had the menus in our hands and as usual i turned to our server, Leishi for recommendations. I never thought we’d end up having a five course dinner here. The recommendations offered by her were all worth a try. Although, the crispy lotus root starter that we wanted was sold out, we were happy choosing the crispy tofu dish instead. The thai ice tea was also unavailable. We chose a thai bubble tea instead. Do ask them to make a dish less spicy, not everyone can handle that kinda thai heat. Our soup, salad and starters arrived fairly quickly and were served well by Leishi. The chicken starter was a fantastic recommendation. The smoky flavour was also a bit like parmesan somehow and it was perfectly cooked.

For the mains, as recommended, we went for the house speciality, green curry with jasmine rice. For me, i got a chicken side dish to go with an extra portion of jasmine rice. I was full but something about the dish made me finish it to the last bit. It was delicious to say the least.

Time for dessert and we thought of skipping it because we were so full! But no! Lets get the sweet potato icecream with sticky rice. 2 scoops resting on sticky rice with some garnish. All gone in minutes. Well recommended by another server.

All in all, we had 5 courses we never thought we’d have. The food was truly authentic with great presentation elevated by some great service. I was very happy at the end.

I will return to try out the unavailable items and many more. Though, I would be on the lookout for some dine-out discounts on swiggy/zomato.

A big thanks to Leishi and other staff that interacted with us. Your warmth and smiles truly made our (parent’s) anniversary dinner exxtra special.

This one will be remembered.
We will return., name_person=Darsh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Went here to get lunch with a friend. The only thing I enjoyed about my experience at The Bar Stock Exchange was the novelty of the drink pricing system. It was interesting to see how the prices of drinks changed throughout the night based on demand. * The place was too crowded and noisy.
* The service was slow and inefficient.
* The drink prices were too high, even during happy hour.

Overall, I would not recommend The Bar Stock Exchange to anyone. There are plenty of other bars in CBD Belapur that offer better food, drinks, and service.

Finally i got a chance to visit this Outlet which is located in Byculla(E).I was so eagerly waiting for the moment to visit this outlet from a very long time.Heard alot of thing about this Restro Bar and wanted to give it a shot.The Outlet is Located just outside Byculla Station on the East side.There aren't any other outlet like Lion Heart in the area which make this outlet special.You come across alot of casual Family Dine In Restaurant in that same area,but Lion's Heart is one of its Kind in Bycula(East).The Restaurant is very easy to spot,but if you are having trouble locating the outlet i would suggest you to take the help of Google Maps which guide you to the exact location.

🔸Talking About The Outlet ➡️

Lion's Heart is one of its kind Restaurant located just outside Byculla Station on the East side.This outlet really lives upto its name and signifies the Lion standing out from rest of the usual Restaurants.Walking in the restaurant feels like you are really walking inside the Lions Heart because of its Premium Interiors and Huge Space.The Restaurant also has Fully Functional Bar along which some Comfortable Lounge and Table Seating.And also on the First floor they have Table seating for pack of 2-4 people along with Live Sports Screening.

Its really remarkable to Operate such a Good Restro-Bar in such a populated area.The Ambience of the restaurant is really Great and Vibrant.The Dim Lighting conditions and a huge screen used for Live Sports Screening which sticks the customers to there seats.The outlet has Indoor Seating which provide ample of comfort and for large grouos they also have Blue Coloured Lounge.

The Restaurant is usually packed on weekends and people come to Enjoy the Nightlife and Live Entertainment of rhis outlet.The food at Lion's Heart is really Taste and Mouth Watering.The outlet offers alot of varieties in North-Indian,Italian and Chinese Cuisines.The most commonly ordered dishes are Butter Chicken,Nachos, Cocktails, Mocktails,Brownie,Biryani,etc.

The staff working at the outlet is extremely professional and knows there work very-well.They are always there to help you and suggest you the best dish as per your taste.The restaurant also offers some board game to play and spend your time with your loved once.They also have a separate Smoking Area.

🔸 Speaking About The Food ➡️

🔰DRINKS/COCKTAILS/MOCKTAILS

◾2)Lady in Red-A Mango base mocktail which i really liked.It was prepared from Mango Juice,Vanilla Icecream and Grenadine syrup at the bottom.The presentation was also upto the marks and pleased my taste buds.
Highly Recommended ❤️

🔰STARTERS/APPETIZERS

◾2)Kataifi Prawns-A prawns base Appetizers which was crispy and a bit of sweet at the same time.The Prawns where marinated and dips in a batter and then fired which made them crispy and so Delicious.The size of the Prawns was really huge and i also liked the sauce which was served along with it.
Definitely you so give it a Try♥️

When dining at The Brasserie, located inside the Hilton at Mumbai International Airport, you’re greeted with a mix of first impressions, starting from the entry itself. The entrance to the hotel can feel a bit cramped, with space limited to accommodate just 2-3 cars at a time on the flat surface, combined with a steep slope for both entry and exit. While valet parking is available, the service felt slightly understaffed, with seemingly only one person managing both the boom barrier and valet parking.

Once past security, you’re welcomed into a cozy and elegant Hilton lobby. Although it’s not grandiose in size, its beauty lies in its thoughtful design. The elegant couches and a glossy white grand piano create a subtle yet refined atmosphere, making it an inviting space. To the left of the lobby is The Brasserie, where we had a lunch buffet.

Ambiance:
The restaurant itself is on the smaller side, accommodating about 50 people. Despite its compact size, the restaurant wasn’t crowded when we arrived for our 2 pm reservation on a Saturday. The place was 80% empty, offering a calm and quiet environment. However, the overall ambiance didn’t exude the level of luxury you might expect from a Hilton property. The seating arrangements were functional but could have been more comfortable, particularly if you’re expecting a more lavish dining experience.

Food:
The buffet featured a wide variety of options, with both vegetarian and non-vegetarian selections available. The spread included:

•	Soups: 1 veg and 1 non-veg option.
•	Salads: 9 different varieties.
•	Starters: 4 options (2 veg, 2 non-veg).
•	Main Course: A mix of Indian and Chinese cuisine, with 4 gravies (2 veg, 2 non-veg), rice, noodles, and a few Chinese gravy dishes.
•	Rice options: Chicken Biryani, Dal Tadka, and Jeera Rice.
•	Non-Veg: Chicken, fish, and egg preparations.
•	Live Counters: Pizza, pasta, and a choice of breads (roti, naan, etc.).
•	Desserts: A decent variety with fruits, pastries, mousse shots, Indian sweets (Barfi, Malai Sandwich), ice creams, and a hot melted chocolate brownie alongside malpuva.

The quality of food was excellent, earning a solid 5/5. Every dish tasted fresh and well-prepared, although the overall taste ranked slightly lower at 4/5, as a few dishes didn’t fully hit the mark in terms of flavor depth. Still, with the wide variety on offer, there was something for every palate.

Service:
The service was decent, but could have been better. With only a few tables occupied, you’d expect more attentiveness from the staff. While they were polite and quick to respond to requests, the overall experience felt a bit lacking in terms of personalized service. For a property under the Hilton name, the expectation of seamless, luxurious service was not fully met, leading to a score of 4/5.

Cleanliness and Ambiance:
The restaurant was clean and tidy, giving off a neat and well-maintained vibe. However, the ambiance didn’t quite match the luxury you’d expect from a high-end hotel dining experience. It was pleasant but lacked a certain “wow” factor that you might anticipate at this price point. This led to a score of 3/5 for both the feel of luxury and sitting arrangements, as these could have been more comfortable and plush.

Overall:
For INR 3,221 per person, including taxes, the buffet at The Brasserie offers decent value if you’re looking for a variety of food in a quiet, elegant setting. The food quality is top-notch, and there’s enough variety to satisfy most diners. However, the experience could be enhanced with a more luxurious ambiance, better seating arrangements, and more personalized service.

Ratings:

•	Food Quality: 5/5
•	Food Taste: 4/5
•	Cleanliness: 4/5
•	Service: 4/5
•	Ambience: 3/5
•	Feel of luxury: 3/5
•	Sitting arrangements: 3/5

This is another excellent recommendation by my friend Shakun. We are staying at Novotel in Juhu, so we enjoyed a leisurely walk on the beach to reach the restaurant. We were welcomed very graciously and seated by the hostess. Since we had walked on the beach and were all very sandy, my husband, my daughters (aged 5 and 7), and I went to the restroom to wash up. When we returned to our table, I was pleasantly surprised to find it set up with a kids’ menu featuring lots of activities, along with sets of crayons and a chef hat crown that both my girls promptly put on. This was such a refreshing change on our 13th day in India, as until now we hadn’t seen a kids menu specifically geared for children in any of the restaurants we’ve visited. It was definitely a highlight for me.

We were kindly greeted by our servers Mukul and Manojit Roy, and their service throughout our meal was outstanding. They offered thoughtful recommendations, anticipated our needs, checked in at just the right moments without being intrusive, and treated our whole family with genuine warmth and respect.

For dinner, both my daughters wanted popcorn chicken—actually their favorite back home—and they were thrilled to see it on the menu. One chose a vanilla milkshake and the other a chocolate milkshake. The popcorn chicken was a bit spicy for their mild palates—but they loved the milkshakes.

My husband and I chose the Fish and Mixed Meats kebab platter. Mukul honestly informed us that the fish was unavailable, and substituted another chicken kebab, which we were completely fine with. We ordered the kebabs as served, thinking our girls might want to try them—and it turned out to be an excellent decision. The girls devoured the chicken reshmi kebab. It was so satisfying to see them enjoying something from the Indian menu, knowing we’ve found another safe and delicious option for them here in India.

We also ordered Rawalpindi Gosht, extra spicy, along with roomali roti and rice to accompany our meal. My husband was delighted with the kebabs—every bite was melt‑in‑your‑mouth tender. The Rawalpindi Gosht was succulent and richly flavored; we absolutely loved it. Despite being full, Mukul suggested the baked motichoor rabri for dessert. It was absolutely delicious—the warm, layered sweetness with the motichoor bits and creamy rabri was the perfect end to our meal.

We loved everything about this place. From the walk-in welcome to the thoughtful touches for our kids, the exceptional service by Mukul and Manojit, and the outstanding food, Copper Chimney Juhu made our evening truly memorable. The serene ambiance and beautiful surroundings make it a perfect getaway from the hustle and bustle of the city. Here's my review of the food and dining experience at City Forest.
To start our meal, we ordered the Chicken Manchao Soup. The soup was flavorful and had a delightful balance of spices. It had tender chicken pieces and was the perfect warm and comforting appetizer to kickstart our culinary journey.
Next, we tried the Bombil Tawa Fry, a popular seafood dish. The bombil (Bombay duck) was expertly fried and had a crispy exterior while remaining tender and moist on the inside. The dish was well-seasoned and served with a tangy dipping sauce, adding a burst of flavor to each bite.
Moving on to the Chicken Lollipop, we were impressed by the presentation and taste. The lollipops were well-marinated, tender, and had a delightful spicy kick. They were served with a tangy sauce, enhancing the overall taste and making it a great choice for chicken lovers.
One of the unique dishes we tried was the Coconut Solkadhi. This refreshing and tangy drink is made from coconut milk, kokum, and spices. It served as a palate cleanser and had a perfect balance of flavors, leaving a refreshing aftertaste.
For the main course, we ordered the Chicken Angara Masala. The dish was packed with flavors and had a smoky and spicy taste. The chicken was cooked to perfection and served with aromatic gravy. It paired well with the Butter Wheat Roti, which was soft, buttery, and a great accompaniment to the flavorful masala.
Overall, our dining experience at City Forest was delightful. The restaurant's serene location in Yeor Hills adds to the charm, and the food served here is flavorful and well-prepared. The staff was friendly and attentive, ensuring a pleasant dining experience.

Cafe Trofima, located near the bustling Shivaji Park in Dadar, has garnered attention as a popular hangout spot, but it falls short of the hype for several reasons.

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very quiet, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=I had great experience and the service was very good the politeness and ambience and food was very good, name_person=Bhavin Chopda}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Toooo Goooddd!!! This place offers so many cuisines that your mind will be confused right from the start. It includes everything from indian and sindhi to mexican, italian and arabic; also offers asian and exotic food items such as fondues. Has a seating area on entry and on the first floor too. Coming to my experience here, it was a mixed review since we had problems related to the air-conditioner and it's management. We sat on the first floor and there's a staircase to reach there. Ambience at both the levels is great and superb!! While the ambience was great, the air-conditioner was equally unrewarding since they weren't working properly. We even reported that to the staff but they said that they already know it's not working and started pretending that they've called the technicians at 4 in the evening the same day!! So even after coming through such scorching heat outside, the inside wasn't much different. Finally after shifting places thrice, we found a spot where cool air could be felt! Apart from all this the food was sooo yummy, fresh and adequate in quantity that my brain didn't have any other issue to focus on!🙌
Food review-
1.Cream of Tomato with Basil soup- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. Also they serve extra croutons if asked for!!🤭
2. Pahadi paneer tikka- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. The paneer pieces were soooo soft and felt really fresh!!
3. Lasagne Ala Napolitano- 3/5 for quantity, 4/5 for taste. Was less in quantity as compared to other places i've had lasagne. Less cheesy as per the standard flavour of lasagne.
4. Dum aloo punjabi- 10/5 for quantity, 10/5 for taste. Reallly reallly very goood in everythinggg from quantity to taste to the dum aloo pieces. Usually 1 potato is provided but here 2 were provided and it's masala and gravy was also soo yummm!!!😋
5. Butter kulcha- 5/5 for taste. Soft, fresshhhh and buttery!!
6. Chinese sizzler- 1/5 for quantity and 1/5 for taste. Typically a chinese sizzler consists of rice, noodles, manchurian balls, chinese gravy and sautéd veggies. But this consisted just of rice, noodles and sautéd veggies. There were no manchurian balls nor there was any gravy which adds to the taste in sizzlers. REALLY A BIG WASTE OF MONEY, I WOULDN'T RECOMMEND YOU TO ORDER ANY SIZZLER AFTER TRYING THIS ONE AS THIS WAS OVERPRICED AS COMPARED TO ANY OTHER PLACE.
7. Basil Citrus Breeze Margarita- 5/5 for look, 3/5 for taste. Looks too fancy and delicious but is just okay. Full of ice and  essence. The management should aeriously think about renovating the place, name_person=Ajay Bhat}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=I've heard about Chulha a lot and been recommended about the same a lot in the last couple of years so I finally decided to give it a visit on my Dad's birthday this year.

The place is quite fancy given the view you get from the 14th Floor. We chose a place near the window and found it extravagant to sit there and enjoy our food.
(Sadly the seats are really uncomfortable. Maybe its a psychological hack that they just don't want the people to enjoy the view endlessly.)

We ordered Chicken Manchow Soup. The soup was quite tasty and not overloaded with garlic which some restaurants do. But sadly the fried noodles were sour. Which I understand was due to the noodles which had turned stale and then they were fried to avoid wastage.

We asked for recommendations from our server and he recommended Banjara Kebab and Dilkhush kebab. But we had already tried those umpteen times in other restaurants so we rather went for Murgh Maharaja Kebab. It was Chicken Tikka Kebab which was in turn wrapped with Chicken Seekh Kebab. We found the description quite fancy and ordered that. Were served 6 pieces of it. Honestly taste was great but wasn't really value for money. And was on the drier side so had to compensate with the green Chutney and lemon.

Then we ordered Java Style Chicken Lollipop which was really tasty. Though there was no hint of Thai flavor in it. It simply felt it was tossed in Schezwan Sauce.

We then saw Sizzlers on the menu and were really tempted to order the same. So we ordered a Chilli Basil Chicken Sizzler. The quantity was humongous. We were three people and initially I thought only 2 would be able to share but the portion size was more than enough for 3 people. Noodles were sadly soggy and overboiled and sauce was a bit bland for my palette. But it didn't matter much it was tasty.

I ordered a Chicken Tikka Biryani and again the portion size was more than enough for 2 people.

Our total bill was around 2200. And I feel it was all in all a good experience.

Only downside being the server being a bit too smart. Servers are generally preferred to be humble but he did talk back to us when we complained about being made to wait for over 30 to 40 minutes for our food even when only one other table was there at the restaurant., name_person=Gaurav Biswas}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=2 years ago, review=We came here after a hike from Karnala fort in the Evening. I feel this place is not recommended if you are dire  hungry. Its a good place for a casual date or for discussion.

The restaurant has both indoor air-conditioned seating and outdoor seating. We chose outdoor seating as air-conditioned seating area was fully occupied. But the tables on the left side did not seem suitable for four people, they were comfortable for only two people.

We started off with their seafood soup, which was practically a treasure hunt in a bowl, packed with so many varieties of seafood that I stopped trying to count after a few spoonfuls. A rich, flavorful start that set the tone for the evening.

Next came the Bombil Fry, and let me say this: if you visit Maaslli and skip this, you’re missing the highlight of the menu. Perfectly crisp on the outside, melt-in-your-mouth inside, it was unanimously the table favorite.

The Prawns Ghee Roast, their signature dish, followed, aromatic, buttery, and spicy in all the right ways. You could taste the freshness of the prawns through the layers of ghee and masala.

I ordered the cucumber mint cooler as a palette cleanser, one of the best non-alcoholic drinks I’ve had. Truly impressed by the bar at this outlet

To round things off, we indulged in the Crab Gravy with Bhakri, a true coastal comfort combination. The gravy had that home-style depth of flavor that only comes from slow cooking and authentic spices.

Between the impeccable flavors, warm service, and the nostalgic coastal touch in every dish, Maaslli continues to set the gold standard for seafood in Mumbai. Can’t wait for next year’s reunion, though honestly, I might not wait that long to go back., name_person=Yogen Sachdev}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Bombil, Pomfret, Prawns_Biryani, Prawns_Lasooni_Fry], GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 months ago, review=Maaslli Restaurant & Bar, at Kemps Corner, Mumbai.
Basically a Sea food Restaurant, but also have other non veg dishes on their platter.
One cannot afford to miss the fried Bombil (Fresh, Fried Bombay Ducks).
They have a great Menu.
They do have various Thali dishes and other alcarte dishes.
It is just mouth watering and thus unable to put in words to describe the dishes.
One must enjoy the crab dishes and crab soup.
They also present you their fresh catch and you may select the fish if your choice, depending upon the weight the rate is fixed.
The atmosphere is damn cool and decent with fishes reflecting in the walls and partisans.
The curry, different types is served and we are asked to taste, then by adding coconut oil again to try. Thus if you are ordering any curry dish you can select your choice of curry.
The staff is very courteous and friendly.
The person, Mr. Anthony, accepting the order is very polite and well versed with the description of the dishes.
Service is quite fast and dishes are very tempting.
The complete crockery is if copper OR may be brass (not sure). But it is a real experience to have your food in such dish and even the fork and spoon.
The soup was something different from the normal ones which all must have experienced.
Crab soup, very tasty and hot enough and goes without saying very tasty.
Sweet dish of Modak and a sweetening dish made if milk and sprinkled with pista, woh! Lovely.
The dishes are well place and economically rated.
If you are in that area, do give a try and taste the tasty dishes, yes! Definitely one have a inclination and a taste for Sea Food.
The Bar is open and you have choices of hard drinks, Cocktails and even Mocktails.

It’s a size ‘S’ place - that too coz of the mezzanine floor - so best to book and go. The whole place has a quaint look and warm ambience.

So, it was 6 of us and we ordered 7 dishes and orange juice.

The chicken and egg roll were tasty, accompanied by a fresh and slightly sweet tomato and onion chutney. They gave sweet potato fries with it; I would have preferred if they gave a choice between regular and sweet potatoes.

The English breakfast was as it should be. The hash browns were crunchy.

The spicy mutton keema with pao was ok. Have had better.

The s’mores waffles looked so pretty and tasted good. Same with the old fashioned pancake. The only thing is these days restaurants don’t serve chocolate sauce with it. It’s an add on which you have to pay for. It’s a peev that my kids have with all places serving waffles and pancakes without chocolate sauce or Nutella. But that not withstanding, the taste was great.

Now coming to the 2 things we didn’t like. The chicken croffles, looked like batter fried chicken breast on a waffle and it looked too dark as if deep fried for too long and didn’t taste well. The other thing was that the juices turned out to be too expensive. That glass cost ₹450 without taxes. Nearly equivalent to a dish. That was too much. And for that size of glass ₹200 or ₹250 would have been good.

This is a Veg restaurant. Just because it’s a veg restaurant they have introduce a lot of innovative dishes to the menu and all. This restaurant is small and cozy with around 7-8 tables with a total sitting capacity of 40 people. This is an old restaurant who has kept them self-updated with latest food trends and drinks. The Ambiance of the restaurant is also smile and plan with nothing much in designs.

The first dish I tried was Aloo Nazakat. This is a small appetizer with a good burst of flavors. It’s a small potato cut in half which is marinated with a spicy marination. Then it is topped with cheeses later baked in grill. I liked this dish mainly because of it size. I would say its like a small boom of flavors. I would recommend you to try this dish and pair it with a sweet mocktail.

The second dish was The Corn Cheese Kurkure. This is a very good veg starters and I would go for this dish over many non-veg starters. This is a crispy dish with a very creamy filling. The inner filling is made up of palak paste mixed with cheese and corn, which is wrapped around spring roll wrap and the entire thing is deep fried until golden brown. This dish is served in shot glasses filled in green chutney and garnished with cheese. You can eat this dish like a finger sticks and its really enjoyable dish.

The Next dish was the Falafal Pocket. This is a middle eastern dish which is prepared very nicely by the restaurant. Basically what this dish is a fluffy form of pita bread which is stuffed with a creamy salad. This restaurant fills the bread with very little salad and serves the rest as side dish so as to fill it more as per your individual needs. They also serve Humus sauce which is prepared by their chef to go along with this dish. The texture of the dish is very tempting wanting you to fill it with more of the salad. If you want something new to eat go for this dish.

Then I went for the Main course in which the first was Panner in Coriander Sauce. This was a nice pan Asian dish prepared with delicate sauce. The Texture of the dish was dark and thick whereas the aroma was very light on the nose. This is a stirred fried dish which is cooked along with spring onion , scallops and herbs. The panner is soft and tender and well submersed in the flavor of the Coriander sauce. A must try dish along with some drink.

Next up was the Dunger Panner Biriyani. This dish was more on presentation then its taste. The texture of the dish was rich and the aroma was very strong everyone in the hotel could smell the dish as it comes to your table.  The dish is mixed with a creamy panners and aromatic rice. This dish is best suited to have it along with a group of people at the end.

The last dish was the Desert i.e. Gulab Jamun Cheese Cake. The cake is exactly as it sounds it to be. This is a cheese cake filled with Gulab Jamun throughout. The food did not live up to expectations. The menu looks promising, but the taste and quality simply don’t justify the pricing. Portions felt inconsistent, and the presentation lacked effort. It’s the kind of food that fills you up but doesn’t leave you with the satisfaction of a good meal.

The ambience is very ordinary, with hardly any attention given to creating a warm or inviting atmosphere. The interiors look dated and basic, giving more of a canteen-like feel rather than a family restaurant. If you’re looking for a comfortable or pleasant dining experience, this place may disappoint.

The service too leaves much to be desired. Staff were slow to respond, not very attentive, and didn’t seem trained to handle customers efficiently. Even simple requests took longer than expected, which made the dining experience drag unnecessarily.

Overall, Bhushan Family Restaurant feels like a place you might step into because it’s nearby, but it doesn’t offer enough in terms of taste, comfort, or service to make you want to return. With so many better dining options in Navi Mumbai, this one doesn’t really stand out.

I recently had the pleasure of meeting Janice, the owner, during my first visit. I was curious to check out the place, and I'm so glad I did. Their butter chicken was absolutely delicious and hit the spot!

We began with soups – some of us chose the Cream of Tomato, while a few went for the Vegetable Manchow. The Cream of Tomato was spot on with its rich yet balanced sweetness, smooth consistency, a drizzle of cream, and crunchy breadcrumbs to top it off. It was satisfying and flavorful. However, the Manchow soup was a bit of a letdown – while it had plenty of veggies, it was extra spicy and lacked that signature tang and flavor one usually expects. Let's start with the positive. The atmosphere is undoubtedly appealing; it's a stylish, modern space with a nice vibe that makes a good first impression. This was complemented by genuinely good service. Our server was attentive, friendly, and efficient, ensuring our glasses were never empty and checking in on us at just the right times.

However, these positives were significantly overshadowed by the venue's major drawback: its size. The place is simply too small for the crowd it attracts. Tables are crammed uncomfortably close together, making private conversation nearly impossible and creating a constant, cramped feeling. The noise level was high, and navigating to the restroom felt like an obstacle course.

Unfortunately, the most disappointing aspect was the food, which I found to be below average. While presented nicely, my main course was underseasoned and lacked the freshness and flavour I expected for the price. It felt like a dish going through the motions without any passion or precision.

In conclusion, Spin City has a great foundation with its pleasant atmosphere and excellent staff. Moving on to the food: In starters, we tried the Hara Bhara Kebab, Punjabi Lasooni Chicken, and Murgh Lucknowi Seekh Kebab — all of which were flavorful and enjoyable. But again, the delay in service really dampened the mood.

Chapati, rice, papad, pickle - perfect.

The prawn thali
The prawns fry - deep fried filled with flavours
The prawn curry - yumminess
Jowar bhakri - wow

(Other stuff was similar to the surmai thali)

The washroom hygenie was excellent. Spic and span clean.

📍 Location & Ambiance
Nock Nock Resto Bar is located in an upscale part of Kalyan, inside Tharwani Vedant Palacia on Vasant Valley Road near D-Mart. The surroundings are surprisingly premium, with well-crafted statues and a high-end architectural feel—something you’d expect in Powai’s Hiranandani rather than Kalyan.

Once inside, the ambiance is pure “mafia boss” vibes. The dark wood interiors, green upholstered chairs, and round tables make you feel like you’re in a high-stakes meeting. The decor is eccentric yet classy, with framed pictures of animals like dogs and lions dressed in blazers, giving a Russian-mafia-meets-gentleman’s-club aesthetic.

🍽️ Dining Experience
We opted for Zomato Dining, which helped us save ₹400 on our total bill of ₹3,000. Ordering food one by one worked well, allowing us to pace the meal and enjoy every bite. The food quality was excellent, with generous portions.

🔹 Food Ordered:
•	Signature Dishes (Detailed pricing wasn’t noted but falls in the ₹400-₹600 range per dish)
•	Drinks: LIT (Long Island Iced Tea) – A strong mix of whiskey, vodka, and rum, giving a solid kick
•	Beer – On the expensive side, so not highly recommended

🍷 Pricing & Offers
The alcohol pricing is steep, so if you’re planning to drink, be mindful of the cost. However, with Zomato Dining, we got a discount, making it a better deal.

👨‍🍳 Service
The service was excellent—staff was attentive yet non-intrusive. They let us enjoy our meal without unnecessary interruptions. For a birthday celebration, they accommodated our request to bring in our own cake and made sure everything went smoothly.

🔍 Final Verdict
✔ Ambiance: 5/5 – Mafia-style interiors with a premium touch
✔ Food: 4.5/5 – Great quality, good portions

However, from the start, the experience left much to be desired. Located at the top of a building, the restaurant had a vibrant appeal, but the ambiance didn’t quite meet our expectations. Despite having a prior reservation through Zomato, the staff seemed unaware and struggled to find us a spot, even claiming the place was fully booked. After some back and forth, they finally seated us at a corner table for four, which was not an ideal start.

The dim lighting was the next major issue – a dark red light directly above our heads cast the entire area in a shadow, making it hard to even see our food. This setup created a rather uncomfortable dining experience, as it felt too dark and disorienting. We began our meal with Loaded Nachos, served with refried beans, salsa sauce, cheese sauce, and sour cream. While the nachos themselves were decent, the salsa and sour cream were surprisingly bland, lacking the zest expected from these toppings. Unfortunately, this combination didn’t appeal to our tastes.

Next, we tried the Cheesy French Fries, and here too, we faced disappointment. Though the cheese sauce was flavorful, the fries were soggy and lacked the salt and crispiness that would have enhanced the dish. It was quite underwhelming, and we found ourselves forcing the dish down. For the main course, we chose the Veg Classic Fried Rice Bowl, which was thankfully a highlight. The fried rice was delicious, with perfectly cooked long-grain rice mixed with fresh vegetables. The accompanying Manchurian gravy with two Manchurian balls was flavorful and well-seasoned, making this dish the only true saving grace of the evening.

Lastly, we looked forward to dessert but were disheartened to learn that the only option was a hot chocolate brownie. This limited choice was disappointing and left us feeling as if options were unnecessarily restricted. To top it all off, the music was unbearably loud, making conversation nearly impossible. Overall, our experience at Bombar was underwhelming, with improvements needed in both food quality and atmosphere. I had the opportunity to have buffet here and unfortunately, the experience fell short of expectations. While the ambiance and service were good, the food was a major letdown.

We regularly come here..as our kids love eating here.
However the price isnt justified with the items Served.

The buffet is with limited items and the dishes lacked the authentic flavors and spices that cuisine is known for. The curries were bland, fish was overcooked, mutton was chewy and uninspired. As an Indian, I was particularly disappointed to see the lack of variety and attention to detail in the preparation of the dishes. Starters were few, like veg crispy-which wasent crispy at all, on top of that it was cold. Chicken tikka was fine. Veg dimsum was readymade packet bought and wasent prepared fresh by the chef.
